Step 1b The institution has left (J-V5.53; item 20 (h)): if reason institution and it is gone (dossier removal at an absorb — leaves at once, building vacated, uses closed §7.7; custom kind deactivated item 104 (e); closed with no successor a whole epoch), the island re-reasons: (i) the next eligible instance of a row tag or archetype relocates up into the vacant claim (ground site handed over by V5 §3.5); else (ii) becomes a prosperity island where h_carried(v(rich)) > 0 and rich demand admits — claim's building re-let as a mansion (relet to rich residential class), rich households taken by demandTaken and relocation within the churn cap, the claim's face keeping its sky-* kind until a re-derivation re-types it sky-island; else (iii) A_t = 0 and it wanes; reason and institution rewritten by the conversion; report and clerk name the cause.

Step 2 Floating: if A_t = 0 waneIsland (floating → waning), dwellUntilWeek = week + a draw in dwellYears.waning × 52 on island.place (lineage + epoch component, index dwell); else if abs(A_t − areaHa) > hysteresis × areaHa resizeIsland toward A_t by ≤ growthPerYear · areaHa · years either way, and altitude toward E_t by ≤ altitudeRateMPerYear · years m, never below V5 §3.9's floor.

Step 3 Waning: altitude falls linearly to V5 §3.9's floor (with E_min) by dwell's end, area toward half its start value, both by resizeIsland; households leave in reverse ordinal order (suffix, as §4.11 (c)), ⌈H · years ÷ dwell⌉ each epoch, each a relet down or vacate, the household entering the displaced pool (cause island); vacant buildings step down the ladder; if A_t > 0 again refloatIsland (waning → floating), dwell cleared; at dwell end settleIsland (altitude at floor, every remaining household into the pool, lights 0, dwellUntilWeek = week + draw in dwellYears.settled).

Step 4 Settled: if A_t > 0 (rung admits) refloatIsland (settled → floating), regrowth-first: vacant stock re-occupied before any ground plot, by the rich bands' delta demand first (demandTaken) then relocating existing rich households up within the churn cap (§4.11), altitude climbing at the rate; at dwell end fallIsland (V5 §3.16).

Step 5 Empty slots: a slot with a live unfallen island is never redrawn; an empty slot re-opens with probability (1 − (1 − redrawPerYear)^years) · chance[k] · h_town (II.6 (4), J-A67.40) on island.place with the epoch component, only if every lower slot is filled; a slot a removed record holds is not empty (never re-opened by an epoch, draws nothing, counts as filled; only undo or a T5 declaration re-filling it when no slot is free releases it; ST-04); an opened slot refloats a settled island first (highest h_carried, ties slot then address), else raiseIsland (S7b's delta fill for the sky, rich delta demand first via demandTaken then relocation within the churn cap, then V5 §3.6-§3.14, districts laid by the unit run at the epoch; no shadeBasis until the next epoch's S6).
Step 6: a rung crossing downward makes every island's target 0: they wane, settle and fall over their dwells, never in one epoch (T8-6).

Step 7 Clearance after growth (sky.clearance, afterGrowth, order 50; C5-47; J-V5.68): every live island re-checked by SKY-F's clearance rule against casters the epoch committed under its solid (V06's raised-way pass and a new stage's S4 raised parts with parapet/channel wall and piers, retaining walls' high-side tops, levelled platforms, buildings — stepped at stack envelope top, a building whose Works starts later in the epoch at its planned finished height, V06 §3.2 step 18); reads V06 EpochScope.built/.raised/.levelled where carried, else every caster under the solid; returns one op {op 'reclearIsland', island, groundRefCm, altitudeCm, elevationRaisedCm} raising groundRefCm keeping elevationCm, raising elevationCm only where the floor fails (fate 'raised clear of the aqueduct' naming the caster); never writes shadeBasis (J-V5.27); draws nothing (T-V5-31 (b)).

Locks at the clearance step: a locked island or a lock on its altitudeCm path holds elevationCm; groundRefCm and altitudeCm still rewritten; where the floor then fails the island stays, conflict listed ('clearance held by your lock') and exempt from the clearance invariant as a held island is from the supply invariant (BCR-V5-11). A locked island or locked state, areaHa or altitudeCm path is held by all steps (§7.2), reported 'held against its supply' when supply is 0 (J-V5.10).

Shade over time (item 102 (e)): each epoch's S6 first writes every live island's shadeBasis from the island as it stands when the epoch begins (before this step changes it), then re-reads every strip, so an island change moves the field one epoch later and uses follow by the engine's lag (V06 schedules drift); the basis persists so save/load between epochs changes nothing (C5-01; T-V5-21 (h)); a fallen island casts nothing from the epoch after its fall; a settled island casts from its floor altitude; an island step 5 raises has no shadeBasis until the next S6 (no strip cast or received; J-V5.72); V06's building mask on its lattice likewise starts at the next field phase.
fallIsland: one convert event as a declared sequence of batches (§4.11), whatever its author; (1) footprint = the island's projected land face in world coordinates (anchor + local ring).

Covered set (J-V5.11): every ground entity with ≥ landfall.coverShare of its face or band inside the footprint: every L3 plot and hinterland LandUse face; every reservation (plaza, market, precinct, park, castle bailey); every way (corridor band); every wall stretch (band) and gate (any Gate kind, by footprint; TV-04); every tower; every bridge or pier deck; with item 110 (C5-53; J-V5.64) every raised span (deck band's plan projection in a ground part ≥ 1) and raised-way pier (footprint), every RetainingWall stretch (band) generated or drawn, every deck plot (face on a bridge, pier, mole or quay deck) — less every locked or pinned entity and the plots holding one (kept content; the ruin laps around).

Relocation first: every use in a covered building or reservation relocated by §4.11's rule for a step that empties a building (a dossier-backed use by the solver's dossier request); every household by §4.7's overflow pass inside the event — in an epoch into V06's displaced pool (cause island) — including households of deck plots that (4) brings down, before their deck falls.

The ground (4a): every covered building demolished (cause convert:fallIsland); every covered plot's use vacant with the ruin treatment (deck plots excepted); every covered reservation left vacant under the rubble; every covered LandUse takes kind quarry, owner commons, source = the landfall decoration (BCR-V5-26) — a surface rubble working that sources no underground quarry system, mine-cavern breach or dig-down draw (item 2; V04's quarry rules read only a quarry without source).

The ground (4b) walls: every covered wall stretch and gate steps down §4.11's wall decline ladder to breached over its covered length, written into the enceinte's condition (file f item 575: knots at the covered length's ends; a dismantled run kept; lifecycle decayed while any run not standing), repaired by V06 (V6 §3.7.5), a state with no edge removed (TT-09); the breached length extended to take in the chord along the trace of every covered tower's and gate's footprint (any Gate kind: main, postern, water, gatehouse, castle, §2.7; TV-04), and a tower or gate covered while its stretch is not has breached written over its footprint's chord alone; Tower and Gate carry no state of their own (draw by their run's condition, stand again with it) (TU-03, TV-04; J-V5.79).

The ground (4c): a covered bridge, pier, mole or quay-platform deck becomes ruined (the deck falls; under a bridge the river stays one L0 face and the way's crossing is closed); every covered way takes surface rubble and routing class track, its prior class written to Way.formerClass (BCR-V6-5) unless it already carries one (a lane V06 downgraded keeps it), until the first epoch whose clearance (§4.11 salvage demand; V06's landfall candidate, ST-13) restores the class (V6 §3.5.2, clears it) or a hand setAttr of class does (clears it too, V6 §2.8) (TR-04; J-V5.73).

Item 110's parts (C5-53): every covered raised span and raised-way pier becomes ruined, and a span whose pier is ruined becomes ruined with it (arches fall with their piers whatever their own cover); a raised way with a ruined span has its crossing closed (no junctions with the ways beneath, so the track fallback does not apply; the ways beneath touched only where the footprint covers them); a ruined aqueduct loses its terminal's supply, a fate ('the fountain in <square> runs dry') read by V06's raised-way pass at its first raisedWays step after the fall (same epoch for an epoch's fall, V06 §3.19.2 (4); next epoch for a hand convert; ST-48); vaults beneath a span follow its state by V04's rule (V05 writes nothing underground).

Every covered retaining wall (generated or drawn) steps to decayed over its covered length (item 245's state, the breach op's result; V06 §3.19.4 (3)), no edge removed, keyed by the wall's lineage address, so a later re-derivation of a generated wall keeps it decayed until an epoch's restoration re-derives it (V06 §3.19.4 (6), ST-10; a drawn wall restored by hand), never 're-derived intact under the rubble' (ST-12).

Every deck plot on a covered bridge, pier, mole or quay deck falls with its deck by item 110 (d)'s least disruption: households relocated first, building demolished (convert:fallIsland), the plot tombstoned with the deck (as V06 §3.19.5 (3) does for a struck deck); a repaired deck re-offers its faces and buildings raised on them are new lineages (V06 §3.19.5 (1), (4); V02 §3.16 (7)); never a vacant plot left on a ruined deck (ST-14); each change a listed fate; no edge of the ground's streets and plots added or removed (tombstoned deck plots' lines excepted), so the plan survives under the rubble.

Landfall record: one ground Decoration kind fallen_island whose members (DecorationMember[], BCR-V5-9; TT-03; J-V5.76) are covered plots, land uses, reservations, ways, retaining walls by Id, and covered raised spans and raised-way piers by raised way and item 244's support keys ({raised, span [a,b]}, {raised, support}) — never a deck plot (tombstoned, a fate); source = the island's address; name = grammar's fallen form; each member leaves in the batch of the op that ends its cover (V6 §3.5.2; J-V6.108); §8.2's fallen row draws rubble over members' faces and bands (raised: span deck band in plan or support ring, BCR-V5-18); walls with towers and gates by their runs' condition, bridges, raised parts, retaining walls by own state rows; footprint parts over water leave nothing and are reported ('sank in <water body>').

F-OUTLINE (base; S7b (5); outline not simple): §5.2's rungs; §13.2's outline property test.

Determinism draws (no new concern; J-V5.12): island.place keyed by town lineage indices slot:k, reason:k (slot openings, reason); island.place keyed by island lineage (+ epoch component at an epoch) indices template, bearing, outline, place, relief, river, underside.kind, underside.depth, underside.apex, access:k, dwell; terrain.noise keyed by the island Terrain (fBm); water.river keyed by the island Terrain (meander knots); field.chance keyed by the island (ε); naming keyed by the island and the landfall decoration.

A removed slot draws nothing (slot:k, reason:k skipped; other slots' indices unchanged); sky.clearance, skyAccessObstacles and the removed-ordinal skip draw nothing; strips and route distance draw nothing (pure functions of committed state, sun samples and dmath §6.5; strips read tiers without roughness); the gradient draws only ε on field.chance; tie rule everywhere (J-V5.12): islands by slot then address, sites and lattice cells by lattice y then x, districts by address; tiers' roughness uses dmath noise keyed by the render key (view data outside every digest, §6.2); raiseIsland keys the island by the town's lineage, slot and epoch (J-A8.61); §6.1's distinctness test already runs a sky-island fixture; §13.3's goldens gain T-V5-15's two sky fixtures.

Shade samples: the base sampler of item 102 (a): sun positions {azimuthCdeg, altitudeCdeg}, nine by default at the site latitude on the equinox, sample points per 32 m cell one (centre) by default; set and layout stated in BCR-V5-15 where item 102 leaves them open; ŝ = horizontal unit vector toward the sun (x east, y north); shadow reach c = min(cot altitude, 8) (§8.4's cap at 8 × caster height) for every model-side source (pass 1 terrain and walls, V06's building mask, the strips), one reach law (BCR-V5-15 (i); J-V5.44); a reader counting 'samples a cell is blocked for' takes the mean over the cell's points (J-V5.42).

The solid from the caster's shadeBasis, never the live island (J-V5.47): undersideTiers(basis, {rough: false}) on the basis's rim polygon, underside, anchor and elevation with roughness 0 (model never reads view data, J-V5.30); no basis = no solid; tier 0 the rim from surfaceTopCm down to elevation − rim, tiers 1..n to the apex (none for flat); each tier's ring rasterised once into a bit mask of shade.ringMaskM (4 m) cells in the island's local frame (scanline fill, centre rule) with span [b_i, t_i] cm above ground datum.

Receivers: onto the ground the field raster's 32 m cells at each sampler point x with ground height g(x) bilinear on the committed terrain as the field reads it (S1 heights with T2 strokes, unlevelled; levelling is a platform datum never a receiver height, so a strip at S10a equals a load's rebuild; BCR-V5-30; C5-54; J-V5.65); onto an island the receiver's 32 m lattice over its land face at its own shadeBasis (anchor, elevation), at terrain height plus that datum; a receiver without a basis receives none; only an island whose apex lies above the receiver's surface top casts onto it (never upward).

The test: x blocked at sample s when the ray from (x, g) toward the sun meets a tier; per tier with t_i > g, tier 0 down: track from x + (max(b_i, g) − g) · c · ŝ to x + (t_i − g) · c · ŝ walked in steps ≤ shade.stepM (8 m) both ends included, each point moved into the island frame (less anchor) and looked up; first hit sets bit (point · suns + s) and ends that point's test for that sample; integer cm and dmath (§6.5) in fixed order: samples 0 → 8, cells row-major, points in sampler order, tiers 0 → n.

The window: only blockable cells tested per sample; corridor = the solid's bounding box swept away from the sun by ŝ · c × [b_n − g_max, t_0 − g_min] (terrain extremes over the frame), in receiver cells, clipped to the raster (F-SKY-SHADE); each corridor cell pre-tested in O(1) at its own height (the ray track across the full span must meet the solid's bounding box, else skipped; exact for the box, J-V5.59); stored window = bounding box of cells passing the pre-test over the nine samples.

When — shade evaluations: each first writes every live island's shadeBasis then computes strips from the bases: SKY's last step (generation and any re-derivation that runs SKY; strips onto islands; ground strips follow at S10a from the same bases); S10a's start at a re-derivation starting after SKY and at or before S10a (before step (i) and every hook; never by pass 2, SL-02); each epoch's S6 for every non-fallen island; ground strips computed once per evaluation at first read (V01 S9b at afterDrivers where registered, else pass 2), held (S9b's and pass 2's the same bits; T-V5-21 (h); J-V5.71); never by an edit, scoped regen or SKY-F (J-V5.27); rebuilt on load/replay from persisted bases (BCR-V5-21).

A ground terrain edit (T2 on the ground key, a §4.11 terrain conversion) moves the receiver not the caster: over its effective scope it re-reads every strip's bits from the unchanged bases with the field it recomputes, so session strips equal a load's rebuild (T-V5-21 (h)); item 110 (a)'s levelling moves no receiver.

The fold: for each ground cell each bit of the daylight mask (pass 1 terrain and wall shade, item 102 (b), (c), and after an epoch V06's building mask on the same layout, V06 §3.4 (6)) is OR-ed with the same bit of every covering strip (counts once, J-V5.38); shade share = popcount ÷ bits (BCR-V5-15); the island-free value (same composition without strips) is what the supply law reads at an epoch; at generation S7b (5) reads pass 1 (no island bits by construction, item 102 (c)); on an island the same fold makes shadeSky with V06's building mask on the island lattice after an epoch (item 102 (b); listed for V06; J-V5.33 as narrowed).

The basis compare: each strip records the §6.2 hash of the bases it read; the shade map view and the clerk compare the caster's with the hash of the same fields read from the live island: equal = field shows the island where it hangs; different = view draws the current strip as pending (the one reader of the live island's shade) and the clerk answers 'The ground beneath will catch up the next time the town changes over time', offering Update shade now (V5 §4.2).

What it amounts to (PLAUSIBLE until T-V5-19): at latitude 50° equinox the nine samples stand at 6.4°, 18.7°, 29.5°, 37.2°, 40°; midday ones reach 1.2-1.8 × caster height, mid-morning/afternoon about 3 ×, first and last capped at 8 ×; an island 100-160 m up blocks cells just north of its footprint for about 3-5 of 9 samples and sweeps west and east for one sample each at the day's ends: a crescent north (south in the southern hemisphere), lowered by a third to a half of item 102's all-day amount; root lengthens, flat shortens (J98).
The one placement solver (§4.7 S10b) places everything on an island in the unit run with item 103's rulebook; V05 adds only that the island is reached by a ride and what an island never carries.

skyRoute(doc, from, to) → {lengthCm, access} (@plat/sky; implementer for S10b's reader, BCR-V5-16; J-V5.36): island point p to ground class c = least over admitted accesses a of d_I(p, attach_a) + transferM + run_a + d_G(foot_a, c); d_I = straight distance × the rung's detour factor (§4.7 street law); transferM = routing.transferM (100 m); run_a = the access's run; d_G = the base's mode distance (§4.7 S10b Supply distances by mode): street (ground class raster at the foot × detour) where foot and class are on the same side of the town wall, else road through the gate (a foot outside the walls reaches inside only through a gate); a class on the island read on the island's own class rasters (built by the unit run's S10b); access = the least sum's access (ties by ordinal), named by the clerk.

Route from a ground point to an island class: the same sum the other way; inside the pooled S10b (before the island's placement exists) the island's class stands at the island's land centroid (§4.1 laziness); after generation the placed plots are used; between two islands: through the ground, both legs, two transfers; a river or sea supply edge never crosses arenas (∞); the conjured river and spring pond carry no trade and satisfy no NEEDS row (J-V5.23).

Admitted accesses: state open (unserved reading included), never closed or ruined; a secret access admits only pulls of classes with clandestine clientele (item 103 (a)); a guarded access only its institution's own supply edges and the law-and-enforcement classes' rows.

Families reading the route distance: SUPPLY (street and road modes), CLIENTELE (dist.market, dist.plaza, dist.gate), COMPETITION and COVERAGE (walking radius — route passes every walking radius, hence one unit), ALIGNMENT, every item 103 (b) signature pair across arenas; nuisance families (EMITS vs SENSITIVE-TO; upwind/downwind) read the straight 3-D distance (horizontal and elevation); upstream/downstream never cross arenas.

(4) An island never carries IslandRule.carry.never rows (V5 §3.5 (3) (a)); (5) landings placed by their accesses never by a pull, their siting facts act on neighbours; (6) a custom kind on an island reads its resolved profile, island institution rows take it by scene archetype; an unplaceable preference reported with closest options (item 104 (d)); (7) the island's own placement is not the solver's (J-V5.34): V5 §3.7's score reads no family, its purpose terms are the island-scale reading of those profiles, V11 writes their values with the profile as provenance.

(8) 'Why is this here' (item 103 (e)): a use on an island names the rows that pulled it; a cross-arena pull names the landing it went through and the route length ('near the mill below, by the east hoist, 340 m by route').

(9) Supply chains across the island (item 104 (h); J-V5.39): an ACTIVE custom chain (every node present) and each dossier activeChains[] (processors resolved by kind family, item 105 (i)) placed as one connected thing by the base's chain rules; (a) the sky fill never carries a chain's RESOURCE node or PROCESSING nodes; FINAL SELLER and CONSUMERS follow the proportional share; exception: the island's own institution that is also a chain node stays and keeps every link by the route.

(9)(b) Links cross by the route: every island-ground link is a street supply edge measured by skyRoute (the last ground node leans to the landing foot of the shortest route, the island node to that landing's top); item 104 (h) (2)'s natures act on the route: perishable short reach holds the ground end close to the landing; bulky water/main-road preferences never cross (∞); a valuable link counts a guarded landing as a secure site and an open public one as none.

(9)(c) Order: upstream first (item 104 (h) (4)); at generation the island unit run reads a ground supplier at the block its S10a allocation holds, the ground pool reads an island node at the land centroid; post-build and epochs read placed plots on both arenas; flow order measured along the route: a chain's island final seller stands at a smaller route distance to its market than the chain's resource does, in at least the share the base's ground-only bar declares (T-V5-24).

(9)(d) Shape (item 104 (h) (3) as revised by item 107 (e)): a chain on two arenas sits close at street scale on the ground and STRETCHES through its landing (one step on its road), never read as close across arenas; named a quarter only past item 72's threshold or by dossier/author, on the ground (V01's reading); no quarter assigned by rule.

(9)(e) Endpoints, services, change, declarations: an import/export endpoint's store stands at the ground's gate or quay (item 104 (h) (6)), never at a landing; a custom service providedBy an island institution sits inside it (item 104 (h) (5)); a chain that deactivates leaves island nodes, pulls removed; one that activates places new nodes upstream first, an island node by the solver's positive placement on the island arena (§7.7 placeAt) — never a unit run, never by moving/resizing/re-deriving an island (item 104 (h) (7)); an author's declaration of a custom kind onto an island is T6 assign with criteria.sky keyed by localUid, held, may place a processing node up (fate 'this chain now crosses the hoist').

(10) Supply web across arenas (item 105 (a)-(e); J-V5.50): (a) binding to the NEAREST provider by the edge's mode (item 105 (a), 107 (c)) measured by skyRoute across arenas, ties by provider address; (b) both ends pulled at the access: an island consumer counts toward its ground provider's weighted centre (item 105 (b)) at the foot of the access its route used, a ground consumer of an island provider at that access's top — never beneath the island; (c) orientation, outputs, hubs act through the same substitution; a balanced class's junction may be a landing (foot/top), scored never forced; (d) an impaired or vulnerable activeChains[] link weakens by item 105 (i)'s status table on the route.

(11) Split works and shops (item 105 (h); J-V5.51): one item on two plots on two arenas, works on the ground by nuisance and input rows, shop on the island by output and clientele rows, Use.branchOf naming the works' use; the route between them is its own link; lifecycle: creation by S10b as one item (pooled S10b the works, island unit run the shop reading works at its S10a block); state/closure/removal reaches both; relocation moves each by its own rows; a fall or delete of the island relocates the shop (works stays); undo restores both; merge back by a map-side declaration (on the ground; up only by an author's held T6 declaration with fate); migration absent branchOf = no split; every cross-arena split reported.

(12)(a) Order and relaxation per arena (item 105 (f); J-V5.52): each arena runs item 105 (f)'s order (anchors, field-driving, source-oriented by depth, balanced, market-oriented) and one bounded relaxation on its own (pooled S10b ground; unit run S10b each island), each reading only the other arena's proxies (island classes at land centroid; ground provider at its S10a block), never the other's placed plots, so both relaxations are byte-stable whatever the interleaving (T-V5-22 (j)); after generation both read placed plots, one arena's relaxation holding the other's fixed.

(12)(b) District term (item 105 (g); SLR2-03; J-V5.75): S7b (1)'s supply term reads a sky pseudo-district as one consumer at its island's land centroid's world point (anchor + outline centroid, fixed by S7b (5)), since feet are sited only at SKY; carried classes' links scored there against allocated providers by the centroid distance V01's χ̃ reads at S7c (V01 V1-3.2 (5)), no route; never past J-A72.46's dispersal.

(12)(c) Near enough (item 107 (b)): a cross-arena link's satisfaction plateaus on the route length: full within the good's comfortM of the summed legs (transferM inside), decaying to 0 at maxDistanceM; (d) spread (item 107 (a), (d), (f)): island districts count as districts for coverage; same-kind spacing applies inside each island district; an everyday service's cross-arena supplier link keeps its generous comfortM; (e) quarters never assigned (item 107 (e)): no island district made a quarter by rule; a dossier QUARTER record or district-defining record binds to ground districts before island districts exist; the author may bind one to an island district by T5 with sky and the record's kind, held with its fate.

Rim as a barrier (item 106; J-V5.49): (1) for item 106 (a)'s closure and every enclosed/sealed test the rim chain is a natural barrier of defensibility class sheer, closure only, no wall (V11 adds the row: barrier kind cliff, class sheer, wall none); the clerk's closure answer names barrier cliff (V10 WhyAnswer.closure); (2) generation never walls an island (no stage lays an enceinte on a sky arena); a prison island's defence is rim + guarded landing.

(3) An author's wall on an island (T3 wall in an enclosure kind with key; drawWall with key) is an Enceinte of closure barrier on the island arena (T3 retaining and T2 terrace edges are never enclosures and lay an island RetainingWall; C5-50): approachable arcs are landing yard frontages, each closed across its inner side by one stretch on the rim strip's setback line (ends anchored on the rim, a tower at each anchor, a gate at the yard's attach), every other rim arc closed by the barrier with zero wall edges; the tool snaps ends to the rim and shows rim arcs in the circuit (item 106 (g)); a stroke along the rim away from a landing is bent at dry run to the landing stretches only ('the drop is the wall here', J-VI.4); a stroke across the interior is an inner wall laid as drawn (§4.8 furniture); the stretch profile (item 106 (c)) grades each stretch; adding/removing an access re-evaluates the circuit by item 22's least disruption (listed fates).

(4) The clerk explains an unwalled rim 'the drop is the wall here'; (5) no-op pin: with item 106's barrier closure and stretch profile off, an author's island wall is the base's ring along the rim strip's line, byte-identical to the base (T-V5-27).

Item 110 scope: the base carries item 110 (a)-(d) via the coherence pass, V01 terraced wards and unit-run levelling, V02 stepped massing and deck buildings, V04 vaults under raised ways, V06 all over epochs; V05's rules are the island meeting points; none changes a ground value while islands are off.

(1) Casters under an island (C5-47): raised deck top with parapet or aqueduct channel wall over the deck's plan and raised-way piers (item 110 (b)); a retaining wall's high-side top and a levelled platform's datum where fill raises it (item 110 (a)); a stepped building's highest massing tier from V02's stack envelope (item 110 (c); V02 §3.15.2, X20); read at SKY, SKY-F, after every epoch's growth, by any edit that adds one beneath; heights are V11's raised-way, terrace and massing-tier rows; the P0 measurement runs with them on.

(2) The island yields, never the city (J-V5.68): no raised part, retaining wall or building is moved, lowered or refused because an island floats above it; groundRefCm rises and elevation follows only where the floor needs it; the raised-way generator treats the projected footprint as open air, only the accesses constrain courses; a caster removed beneath re-reads groundRefCm and never lowers the island (V5 §4.3).

(3) Accesses and decks (C5-48, C5-49; J-V5.60, J-V5.61): (a) feet on part-0 land only (admissible ground excludes raised-way pier footprints, raised deck plans dilated by deckGapM, item 110 (d) deck faces); (b) rope lines keep lineClearM over every raised deck and pier crossed, at SKY and after; (c) for every raised part laid after SKY, skyAccessObstacles is read by its two callers (BCR-V5-29 (e)): item 110 (b)'s course solver (at an epoch's raised-way pass, a new stage's S4 in an epoch, 'or at a generation stage after SKY if the integrator places one there') keeping deck, parapet and piers out of every column dilated by deckGapM and under every segment by clearCm, re-routing by its ladder else not building the part ('would cut <island>'s hoist'); T4 road's raised dry run (and the aqueduct class) re-routes or ends the course at its last ground vertex before the column ('this would cut <island>'s hoist; it ends here', J-VI.4 (f)); an access placed or moved later meets standing raised parts by (a) and (b) at its own dry run.

(3)(d) No raised way reaches an island: a raised part's ends are ramps or stairs to ground vertices (item 110 (b)); a T4 raised or aqueduct stroke ending on an island's rim makes no way and is bent into a sky access (J-VI.4 (d)), so II.1's 'sky: no portals, no roads in or out' stands; no raised part stands on an island (decks in ground parts ≥ 1; sky has one part per island); a T4 raised or aqueduct stroke on an island's key is bent (J-VI.4 (e): raised dropped, aqueduct made a fountain pin; lines 'An island carries no raised way; its bridges cross its river on their own decks', 'An island's water is its own'); no access is a way.

(4) Island's own retaining walls (C5-50; BCR-V5-27; J-V5.69): V01's unit run levels island ground by item 110 (a)'s thresholds (terrace.slopeMin, terrace.stepMinCm, V11 rows unchanged); a terraced edge only where the relief class asks (terrainEcho.reliefClass for own; plain for echo and none; V01 V1-3.17.7 (2)); each retaining wall raised or drawn (T3 retaining, T2 terrace edge with key) is a RetainingWall on the island arena; never on the rim strip or along the rim (levelling stops at the setback line; a stroke meeting the strip or running along the rim moved inward past the rim walk: 'The rim walk stays level; the wall stands inside it', J-VI.4 (g)); never an enclosure, never snapped to the rim, never in a barrier circuit; draws in the island frame, displaced under offset (§8.4), shadow on its low side; tombstones at a fall; exports in the sky collection; surface top and crypt re-test read levelledGroundCm; a way crossing it becomes a stair or ramp by item 110 (a)'s way-class rule.

(5) The raised-way generator's reads of the sky (C5-52; J-V5.63; BCR-V5-29 (b)-(d)): (a) an elevated road's endpoints are reservations (citadel site, great temple or cathedral precinct), never the institutions in them; the handover keeps the reservation, so a road raised to a precinct whose cathedral rose stands ('links the citadel and the old cathedral close, whose cathedral rose to <island>'); (b) ground arena only (PlatKey.layer 'ground', any part) for endpoints and evidence, never a sky ward, island institution or island landmark — by arena, never by a list of sky-* kinds; (c) the aqueduct's water need at generation reads the S2 population whole (a small deterministic overestimate, ≤ 3 × H_d per island), at an epoch ground households only; no aqueduct serves an island; (d) the source search reads S1's ground springs and rivers only; no aqueduct terminal, basin, cistern or fountain on an island.

(6) Stepped massing and deck plots on the island (C5-55): an island institution may take V02's stepped rows (stepped temple, terraced palace, tiered tower); the surface top reads each point's highest massing tier; a cathedral's crypt lies under its lowest massing tier inside underside tier 0; the island's bridges (built by V01's unit run) may carry deck plots by item 110 (d) and fall with the island.

(7) Removals: a removed generated raised way, retaining wall or deck plot beneath an island holds by the base's and V06's rule (critique-V6 C6-38); V05 adds only the island's own removals (island or access stays removed). (8) The landfall covers raised spans, raised-way piers, retaining walls and deck plots (V5 §3.16 (2)-(5); C5-53).

(9) No-op pin and declared shift (C5-56; J-V5.67): with item 110's terrace, raised-way and deck-plot rows off every island value (altitude, ground reference, accesses, strips, landfall) is byte-identical to the volume without item 110; with them on at their defaults (owner's ~23:40 default at CITY and METROPOLIS) both sky goldens of T-V5-15 change once, a declared shift naming both fixtures.

Tools on the sky (item 101's twelve, no thirteenth; each at most one new parameter, §7.1): T1 intend (islands setting, count → adjust('layers.islands'), adjust('islands.count'), Re-derive from S7b with fate report §7.8); T2 ground (island terrain, water, rim with new key parameter; terrace stroke laying an island RetainingWall → setField(terrain), drawWater, moveCourseKnot, warp on its key (fromLevel 0 moves the rim), item 110 (a)'s terrace form with key); T3 wall (key; enclosure kind → barrier-closure enceinte walling only landing yards; retaining kind → island RetainingWall, bent inward from the rim (J-VI.4 (g)) → drawWall with key); T4 road (stroke to a rim → placeSkyAccess; raised bent into an access; aqueduct ended at last ground vertex; on an island key raised dropped and aqueduct a fountain pin, J-VI.4 (d)-(e)); T5 quarter (new sky parameter → quarter with sky, sugar expanding to convert raiseIsland (declared), assign and setAttr(name)); T6 place (assign with criteria.sky); T8 fill (brushes with key → setField with key); T9 shape (altitude, area, position, occlusion, underside, field target; access kind, role, state, knowledge, foot; rim handles → setAttr, moveVertex); T10 hold (lock, pin, revert, regenerate with island scope; New random; Update shade now → regenerate scope shade); T11 name (setAttr(name), moveLabel, hideLabel); T12 dress (setLayer('sky', …)); history (convert resizeIsland, waneIsland, settleIsland, fallIsland, refloatIsland, raiseIsland, removeIsland; reclearIsland is the epoch's own with no tool).

Every declared thing is held (§7.2): a declared island's outline and position, a declared altitude or area, a placed access. No tool for the shade or the route (derived, no edit kind); w_sun and the shade, routing, casterAllowanceM cells are table values (editTable §7.6, re-deriving from SKY for casterAllowanceM, S10a for shade, S10b for routing); T8's prosperity brush overrides the field beneath an island as anywhere (item 102 (f)).

New/extended events (BCR-V5-10): placeSkyAccess {island, top PointCm local (snapped at dry run), foot PointCm world, kind?, role?}; quarter gains sky? {altitudeCm?, institution?} (points are world points); point-form events gain key?: PlatKey (default ground): drawWay, drawWater, drawGreen, drawBoundary, drawFootprint, drawWall, placeLight, setField (terrain, prosperity, density, greenery) — points in that arena's frame, converted by the anchor at the dry run; regenerate gains scope {kind 'shade', island}.

ConversionOp island kinds (§4.11) become: resizeIsland {island, areaHa, altitudeCm}; waneIsland / settleIsland / fallIsland / refloatIsland {island}; raiseIsland {allocation?, declared? {ring PolygonCm local, anchor, kind, altitudeCm?}}; removeIsland {island} (record kept in state removed, holding its slot); reclearIsland {island, groundRefCm, altitudeCm, elevationRaisedCm} (returned by sky.clearance only).

Pointing at an island: every sky hit test and tool point converts the pointer's world point to the island frame by the anchor — under offset occlusion first un-displacing it (world point less elevation × offsetPerMetre offset vector, §8.4) — so a click on a lifted island's drawn house selects it (listed for V09's hit testing).

Moving an island (setAttr(anchor), T9 drag): arena untouched; dry run re-reads groundRefCm and the altitude floor, re-checks V5 §3.7's gap and frame, re-lands every access (vertical foot follows its top; slanted keeps its foot while within run, else re-sited by V5 §3.10 (4)); a foot leaving its landing plot closes that plot's sky_landing use (item 17 closeUse, house vacant) and opens one under the new foot by positive placement (§7.7 placeAt); fates list both plots; placement.byAssignment becomes true.

Resizing (setAttr(areaHa) or resizeIsland): rim eroded/dilated by the kernel buffer (§3.7) to the new area within 1 % (bisection on distance, ≤ 12 steps), keeping shape, never re-drawn (J-V5.7); growth past 1.5 × areaHaMax first grows the frame; tiers re-scale (depthCm by square-root area ratio).

Resize: the rim's L1 pieces follow in the same commit (SLR3-02; J-V5.77): one island L1 batch re-lays the rim strip rimStripM inside the new rim and re-claims each landing yard at its re-seated top (where d_k now leaves the land face), the foot re-landed as a move; each re-claimed yard served in the same commit (sky_landing_top plot re-cut, old tombstoned, use opened by placeAt, covered plots re-derived by §7.3's local operator, SKY-F's checks and repairs run on the island).

Resize institution claim: kept where it still fits the land less re-laid strip and yards, else re-searched by V5 §3.10 (5)'s score and crypt re-test inside the district that holds it (every district keeps its kind), that district re-derived by its scoped re-derivation from S8 with the new claim a hole (V01 V1-3.10.3 (6) (c), releasing the institution from V1-3.9's fixed inputs), its S10b placing the institution on the new claim (use relocated, dossier-backed by the dossier request, old building demolished, a fate); re-derived whether or not it receives a band face and once where it does; a resize never leaves the claim without a site: area floored at the least area at which some site in that district fits; a hand request below is bent ('<island> keeps room for its <institution>; shrunk to <area> ha', J-VI.4); an epoch's resizeIsland stops at it, listed.

Shrinking: every plot losing ≥ half its face to the eroded rim, re-laid strip or re-claimed yard is cleared (households relocated on the island first, then to the ground), the rest re-cut with neighbours fixed (§4.7 S10 (7)); every way crossing the re-laid strip line is cut back to it; no district re-derived but the claim's where re-searched; rim walk re-laid by V01 plantRimWalk in the same commit.

Growing: land between old and new strip lines (with whatever an old yard held its re-claim does not, less re-claimed yards) cut into faces by extending, in the same L1 batch, each district boundary way meeting the old strip line across the band along its normal (same class); each face joins the district of its nearest rim stretch (ties by address); every receiving district re-derived by its own scoped re-derivation from S8 (V01 V1-3.10.3 (6) (c)) — never a unit run, never a change of district count; plantRimWalk re-plants the rim walk whole once.

Altitude (setAttr(altitudeCm)): the record alone; a value below V5 §3.9's floor is bent to the floor, the line naming it (J-VI.4). Underside and occlusion setAttr: the record alone (underside.source edit); an underside change breaking the floor raises the altitude (a fate). Field setAttr(field.prosperity) (declared target, gradient shifted), field.density, field.greenery and island brushes (setField with key): island plots whose value crosses a cut past τ re-derive (§7.2), on the island only.

Plain words: a town lives through time from a stated future ('grow by a third over fifty years', decline then recovery) or the SettlementForge dossier week by week; same seed; nothing re-rolled; every surviving house keeps shape and name; only what the year changed changes.

Plain words growth: fill first (empty houses, ruins repaired or rebuilt on old foundations, gaps along old streets), crowd next, spread last along main roads; suburbs large, rich and endangered enough get a new wall and join; the old wall loses purpose (gates opened into squares, stones robbed, becomes a ring road or dissolves into plot backs).

Plain words decline: leave exposed edges first (undefended suburbs, damp ground, tannery streets); empty houses lose roofs, ruin, robbed for stone; empty plots to gardens, orchards, fields; lanes to footpaths; street and wall lines stay; fields to pasture, common, woodland and back; a shrunken defended town may build a shorter wall; uses close and reopen where customers are; apothecary one per district; tannery drifts downstream; rich drift sunward and away from island shade; custom institutions keep places; broken chains drift slowly; quarters only when grown or declared.

Plain words trade: each shop tied to nearest supplier and buyers, ties move the same year, pull both ends; everyday services spread; butcher may split and merge back; a dossier range '5-10 blacksmiths' is honoured, more as the town grows, never below five.

Plain words walls follow ground: new or shorter rings use cliffs, gorges, deep water as wall; a port keeps a gate onto its quays; a campaign town gets new walls only when its dossier says so. Crossing a size keeps its promises: a town growing into a city gets its sewers that year; a village can grow into a town; a shrunken town can become a village again.

Plain words raised ways: a city may raise an aqueduct, viaduct or raised road, each with its reason; a removed one stays removed (undo brings it back); people under arches re-housed that year; disused ones decay (arches fall, piers stand for centuries) and are repaired before anything new; terrace walls outlast their houses, slump only after a generation of abandonment; houses on a bridge burn in turn, a flood that sweeps a bridge takes its houses, rebuilt bridges get new houses.

Plain words underground: caves and buried ruins under any settlement from a hamlet up, sealed and unknown; each new house over one has a small chance of breaking through; a sewer or mine growing into a chamber opens it; deliberate digs; squatters, hermits, an undercity move in only once a way in exists and leave if the last way collapses; deep chambers mostly stay secret; catacombs only under cemeteries (and a big city's quarry ossuary), grow, never shrink, bones stacked tighter; churches get crypts, the cathedral the largest, a moved seat gets its crypt that year.

Plain words hazards: house fire spreading along timber rows until a wide street or stone house stops it; flood on low ground; a tower falls; after a great fire or flood sometimes the ground is raised and rebuilt; a SettlementForge town has only the calamities its dossier reports striking where named; a standalone town small ones by chance and large ones only on request.

Plain words weekly clock: every change shown as it happens (staked out, walls rising, roof framed, emptied, stripped, rubble, overgrowing); a time bar scrubs the whole history; every change a recorded inspectable event ('why did this inn move?') kept with the map; undo while latest; branch ('what if'); the card previews end state and houses gained or lost; anything the history does can be done by hand; locked or pinned things are left alone.

AdvanceRequest {trajectory, from? 'now' or {founding: population}} — not a log event: appends epoch events one per cadence step in one group (BCR-V6-11); from founding = the 'grow from a founding' macro (V6 §3.3.3): in the creation flow it applies to the new document; on an existing document it bends (J-VI.4; ST-35) to 'Start a new town small' (a new document at the founding population under this recipe, advanced; the present one untouched; dry run names the bend). Provenance on each appended epoch (BCR-V6-9): EpochInputs.advance {group, index, of (planned count), stoppedAt? (last epoch only when Stop ended early), trajectory? (index 0 only)}.

Time card and clerk shapes → trajectory: grow (share over span) → rate perYear = (1 + share)^(1/spanYears) − 1 via dmath.pow; reach → target logistic; decline → rate with the negative share or target below the present, logistic; hold → rate 0; timeline → points through circumstance entries beyond the document's week (V6 §3.3.4); the clerk's three variations of a target change: logistic, linear, front-loaded (rate perYear = (T/P0)^(1/spanYears) − 1, most absolute change late for growth and early for decline); the card's more pane and the clerk's advance accept trajectory.slice's threat (0-1) and era row (C6-29).

advance is refused on a dossier-bound document: the host's clock owns its time (§4.11 The clock; J-V6.2); the refusal offers 'Make a what-if copy and advance it' (forkAt at the head, detached, V6 §4.4).

HazardRow {kind (data: fire, flood, collapse …), operator burn/inundate/topple, params (operator defaults; an event's params override), spontaneous? {perYear, mode minor/full (the lowest evolution.hazards setting that admits it)}}. Defaults (our own, calibratable): fire — burn, spontaneous minor, V6 §3.11.2's parameters; flood — inundate, spontaneous full only on a river or coast town, perYear 0.02; collapse — topple, event-only; an unknown kind reported and ignored (V6 §3.17).

A suppression (LifecycleEvent.detail.suppress, BCR-V6-24): create the delete of a generated raised way, harbour-mouth chain, quay wall, retaining wall (key its chain's lineage address) or deck plot (key its host's id and slot ordinal; ST-15), written by the delete operator when the entity's lifecycle cause is a generation or epoch rule; read RaisedWayLedger and the fortification phase's waterfront rule every epoch, the retaining-wall re-derivation, tier (5)'s deck faces, generation's S4, S6, S10-S11 and a new stage's S5b (BCR-V6-25), rerunFrom's re-apply, V10's 'removed by you'; persist model data identity layer on the delete's lifecycle event; regen read again at every regeneration (the log's live removals replayed; generator skips the key); undo lifted only by the delete's undo or a forkAt before the removal; served (never generated again, counted once) while the user's re-add stands, per kind as V6 §3.19.3 (3), (7) name the forms V9 §4.20.3 (4)'s Build it again emits (drawWay raised, drawWall, placeGate, drawWall retaining, drawFootprint on the deck; SR3-08), deleting the re-add leaving the removal in force; absent in older documents.

(harbourChain: enceinte and harbour basin; quayWall: enceinte and water body of its waterfront arc), chain? (retaining: deleted wall's chain lineage address), host?, slot? (deckPlot: host id, item 246, and slot ordinal from its host's first end)}; islands and sky accesses keep V05's record form (SkyIsland.removed, .removedAccesses) under the same lift rule (f item 260; ST-15, ST-59).

The ledger is a pure function of the model and the log: suppressed set = the suppress of every live (not undone) delete of kind raised (other kinds read the same way by their own generators: waterfront rule, levelling's walls, tier (5)'s deck faces); counts read the standing raised ways' reason and lifecycle cause; exported by the package holding the base's raised-way generator (BCR-V6-25), called by the pass (V6 §3.19), generation's S4 and S6 and a new stage's S5b, so no generator can exceed a cap or re-found a suppressed reason on any path.

Runner (1) Checkpoint: the session takes §7.4's checkpoint before the epoch; the history index gains the epoch's entry. (2) Strategy: read evolution.strategy from the effective parameters at the epoch's log position and look it up in StrategyRegistry.evolution (§14); an adjust grow-by-stage → history applies from the next epoch (dry run: 'from the next year the town's history runs in full; the years already recorded stay as they are'); fields older epochs never wrote read as their defaults.

'grow-by-stage' is the base's built path: registers a phase for every step the base runs — prelude (rung and dials before S2), demand (S2), field ((a) as M4 builds it, without the building mask), dossier ((e)), siting ((f)), growth ((g)), lapse ((h)), character ((i)), works ((j)) — reproducing M4's path byte for byte (T-V6-1 the arbiter: a step M4 runs with no phase fails it); base phases built once in @plat/edit; 'history' reuses them for the steps V6 §3.2 marks base (prelude's base part, demand, dossier, lapse, character) and wraps the base parts of field, siting, growth, works with its own acts (one code path; J-V6.1).

Runner (3) Context: EpochContext built once — seq the epoch event's, week = inputs.week (§4.11 The clock (1)), prevWeek (previous epoch's or the creation week), years = difference ÷ 52, the churn ledger from §4.11's caps scaled by years, product and rung from V07 §2.1's fold (BCR-V7-26; the previous epoch's product runs unless the target crossed 1 575 upward or 1 425 downward, reading its own rung row at its edge inside the band; ST-01, J-V6.97), the household ledger empty.

Runner (4) Phases: per EpochStep in order: the product's override when the epoch's product declares one in ProductDecl.phases (V07's village declares siting and growth), else the strategy's; a step with neither runs nothing; then at afterField, decline, afterGrowth every registered EpochParticipant of that step (the product's included, whatever the product; scoped ones gate themselves; TW-08) in (order, id) order; the runner commits ops in the order given as single-level batches of this one event (§3.3), each through the same operator a hand convert or edit uses (§7.1) — one code path; routes displaced rows into the ledger (writing Household.transit) and demandTaken into ledger.take; an op the operator refuses (a conflict the filter could not see, a kernel invariant) is skipped and reported (V6 §3.17); the next op runs on the state left.

Runner (5) Close: asserts the ledger's pool is empty — a household still in it (a phase failed after displacing it) is housed by the overflow ladder's last rung (V6 §3.6 (2)) inside close's own batch and reported — then writes the EpochReport to the report block; EpochRecord.postDigest = the model digest after the last batch (§2.9).

Protection: every candidate list excludes what §4.11's exemptions exclude — a locked or pinned entity never struck, converted or moved; an assigned entity moves only through the use step; a dossier-backed use's building emptied or removed only after the use is relocated — except the targets a mapped calamity names (struck where they stand, V6 §3.11.1); a church-family use whose plot holds a churchyard and a singular use (the cathedral among them) are never moved by the use phase (V6 §3.9.5; J-V6.66); a removed generated raised way, harbour-mouth chain, quay wall, retaining wall or deck plot is never re-founded (suppressed; ST-15); the filter runs before the draw, so a protected entity never consumes a draw or a cap (J-V6.7).

Purity: the engine reads the committed state, the epoch's inputs, the tables pinned in the recipe and the log, and nothing else (no view key, wall clock or host call), so a replay reproduces every epoch (§6.2 Histories, not states).

Phase order (base (a)-(j) with four additions, BCR-V6-1): 1 prelude (before S2: product and rung from the fold; dials past hysteresis, TradeFlow re-read; slice and wealth level; feature set re-resolved) base + V6 §3.3; 2 hazards (calamity hazard events with F5 targets in place, timeline events, spontaneous hazards; burn, inundate, topple; raiseGrade; households into the ledger) V6 §3.11; 3 demand (S2 delta) base; 4 field ((a): building shade mask written, then S6 re-evaluates drivers, re-bands fieldBand, marks due blocks, re-lays the surface of each way whose fronting band crossed the hysteresis by V1-3.7.3, an edited surface kept) V6 §3.4 + base + V01; 5 afterField (sky.islands, village.plan, village.density); 6 uses ((b): strain, closing, opening, relocation, coverage; MutationPlans) V6 §3.9; 7 departures ((c) first half) V6 §3.5.1; 8 decline ((c) second half: strike lottery over building, plot-boundary, street, raised-span, retaining-wall, deck candidates; participant under.fade) V6 §3.5.2 + V04; 9 fortification V6 §3.7.2-§3.7.6; 10 terrainWater V6 §3.12; 10a raisedWays V6 §3.19; 11 ladder ((d) + MutationPlan steps due) V6 §3.8.4, §3.10; 12 dossier ((e) + product records placement + V6's readings) base + V6; 13 siting ((f): pool, then delta less taken, regrowth-first with V6's tiers) V6 §3.8; 14 growth ((g): crowding hook, growth decision on residual and backlog; a new stage through S5-S13) V6 §3.6, §3.7.1; 15 afterGrowth (under.extend, under.access, under.undercity, hood.fabric, sky.clearance, village.pins); 16 lapse ((h)) base; 17 character ((i)) base; 18 works ((j): a Works for every building-level physical change of steps 2-15, start weeks spread; retirement) V6 §3.13; 19 close (report, chronicle, history index) V6 §3.15.

Dossier step (12) detail: each assign the step places (a record added, a member a count step adds, or the greater a REPLACEMENT re-key places new; V08 §3.5.1 (c), (d); V07 §3.12 item 4; SR5-02) is offered first, at an epoch whose product declares one, to the product's records placement, which places or declines it to the base's placement (§7.7 One path; TV-02); a re-key whose greater keeps the lesser's thing (V08's first case) is a rebind, never offered or placed (V6 §3.9.11 in-place convert; TX-06); keyed by the adding event's seq (TW-01); each record removed handed after the base's removal to that placement's remove (TW-02); then V6's readings: ladder steps (V6 §3.9.11), activeChains re-bound, a walls record's circuit trigger (V6 §3.7.6 (4)), a see's crypt (V6 §3.18.3 (1)).

Participants (each runs at every epoch at its step whatever the product; a scope is its own gate returning no ops outside it; J-V6.124): afterField 0 sky.islands @plat/sky — V05's IslandEpochStep, every island event an epoch can run at every rung where an island stands (TOWN's carried or declared islands included): raise (S7b's delta fill, SKY's island steps, districts laid by V01's unit run inside the epoch's commit), resize (growing or shrinking, V05 §4.2's whole resize in its own batch: rim L1 pieces re-laid, yards re-claimed and served, feet re-landed, claim kept or re-searched, shrink's plots cleared and re-cut, growth's receiving districts re-derived, plantRimWalk), wane, settle, refloat, institution re-reasoning (relocate or relet), fall with landfall — each priced per event in V6 §6.2 at V05 §6's row (SLR3-11, TU-06 (a); TV-01, SLR4-09); afterField 10 village.plan (scope village rung; V07 §3.12 plan re-read); afterField 20 village.density (scope a document holding a superseded VillagePlan under any product; ST-28; VS2 density re-derived on the old core's recorded inputs); decline 10 under.fade (V04 UndergroundFade; ruins' decay at RuinRule.fadeFactor; a lived void whose last access seals vacated in the same batch).

Participants afterGrowth: 10 under.extend (V4 §3.10's one order, TR-18: first Foundations.apply(doc, scope, cause) (V6 §3.18.1 (6); ST-20); then ArchVaults.reconcile(doc, scope.raised, epoch); then SewerStrategy.derive (U-NET whole) the first epoch Features.sewers turns on, else SewerStrategy.extend with U-NET's invert drops at the wall crossings of ways in scope.levelled (C4-110-7); then CatacombGrowth.grow with opts (cap, primary, calamity deaths) with crypt joins inside; then QuarryWorkings.extend (TOWN and above); at a village rung V04's maintenance mode: no sewer extension, no catacomb growth (blockedBy 'rung'), no new working — foundations and arch-vault reconcile only); 20 under.access (AccessPass.run over the scope; excavation by demand; at a village rung tests caverns, ruins, workings, openings only, no excavation; ST-18); 30 under.undercity (UndercityEpoch.reread, then F6's scattered void dwellings filled by relocating the district's poorest-band ground households; vacated households re-housed inside; ST-19); 40 hood.fabric @plat/hood (V01's S7c on districts created outside S7b, S9b on blocks in scope.recut; districts a part in scope.raised crosses: fabric reading and hood pins re-derived over the committed plot set, no plot removal, no re-homing; ST-53, ST-54); 50 sky.clearance @plat/sky (V05's rule after growth; elevationCm kept, raised only where the floor fails; shadeBasis never written); 60 village.pins (scope village rung; VS8's pin rows by least disruption; TV-03).

The arch-vault reconcile (ArchVaults.reconcile, V4 §3.5.4 (d); in under.extend after the foundations and before the sewer's extension so its chambers are in scope.elements for under.access in the same epoch): for every raised way in scope.raised, in address order, V04's arch-vault source is brought to the way's present state — a chamber laid for each standing vault span without one, a chamber under a ruined or cleared span collapsed, every chamber of a removed way deleted with its links and accesses (C4-110-3); breach, dismantle and removal ops already do so in their batch (BCR-V6-26) and the hand operator lays a new part's chambers, so the reconcile is the one epoch-side guarantee.

'grow-by-stage' registers no participant of its own; participants run under it when their packages are loaded — a product's phases, participants and records placement at file f item 202's call points with the ProductEpochContext the grow path fills (V07 BCR-V7-18; TX-02); the @plat/evolve adapters live only for 'history', and under grow-by-stage V04's own M4 hooks stand for V04's functions (V04's U5, V04 §8).

Feature set at an epoch (BCR-V6-16; J-V6.60): after the fold's rung is read, the prelude re-resolves rung-decided features (II.7.1): at CITY and METROPOLIS Features.sewers turns on; at TOWN the creation's one uniform u on blueprint.features (S0's, no new draw) is compared with the TOWN law's probability at the epoch's population and wealth, turning on the first epoch u < P(epoch) — deterministic, monotone in population, cadence-independent, equal to creation's result at creation's population; once on, never off (item 11); a requested off at CITY is the base's hidden layer; at a village rung (a town handed down) the feature stays on and the network is held in V04's maintenance mode (silts and caves by under.fade, never extends; ST-18); the first epoch it turns on, under.extend lays the whole network (U-NET over current ways), reported (under.featureOn) and chronicled; caverns and ruins need no re-resolution (item 109 (j) (1)); the catacomb count reads the rung each epoch.

Why this order: hazards before demand (displaced households and burned plots known to every later step); fortification after decline and before siting (land a ring road or absorbed wall frees is offered to tier (5) the same epoch); terrain and water with decline, before siting (reclaimed land can take growth); use step before departures (J-V6.8); under.extend before under.access (every element grown tested for overlap the same epoch); under.access before under.undercity (an opened access may start dwellings, item 109 (j) (4)); a crypt needs no participant (re-derived inside the op changing a church's designation); raisedWays after terrainWater, before ladder (cleared plots rung-3 eligible), before siting (displaced re-housed, none to a tent, J-V6.82), before afterGrowth (under.extend lays vaults, hood.fabric re-derives crossed close-ups, sky.clearance at order 50 reads them).

Dossier-bound inputs (3.3.1): the port folds epochs by §4.11's cadence (a 52-week boundary, or a population move past the roster tolerance) with the week, target, slices, calamity records (typed by V6's calamity table, DR-V6.1, BCR-V6-12), wealth level (DR6, BCR-V6-9) and that week's dossier events; the engine invents none (population target, slices, calamities are the dossier's; everything else derived, item 20 (h)); advance refused (J-V6.2) offering the detached what-if copy; spontaneous hazards none by rule (J-V6.19).

Standalone advance(trajectory) (3.3.2): expands before anything is appended into n = ⌈spanYears × 52 ÷ cadenceWeeks⌉ epochs; above advance.maxEpochs it bends: cadence = ⌈spanYears × 52 ÷ advance.maxEpochs⌉ weeks, said in one line ('a 500-year history runs in 130-week steps'; item 101 R2 bend); with W0 the document's week and P0 its population (last epoch's populationTarget, else the recipe's S2 population), epoch i at W_i = W0 + min(i × cadenceWeeks, spanYears × 52) (integer weeks, spanYears × 52 rounded half-up), f_i = (W_i − W0) ÷ (W_n − W0).

Population per epoch: rate P0 × (1 + perYear)^((W_i − W0)/52) via dmath.pow; target/linear P0 + (T − P0) f_i; target/logistic P0 + (T − P0)(L(f_i) − L(0))/(L(1) − L(0)), L(f) = 1/(1 + e^(−8(f − 0.5))) via dmath.exp (8 our own); points piecewise linear in the week, P0 before the first, last after; each rounded half up and clamped to the union of the registered products' ladders (§1.1's router): [1 500, 120 000] with the town product alone, [0, 120 000] with V07's village product registered (0 = V07 §3.12's deserted outcome), a clamp reported (J-V6.5, J-V6.61); an epoch whose product the fold changes (village → town at 1 575, town → village below 1 425) runs that product's phase overrides.

Slice, wealth, events per epoch: the slice = the current (last epoch's, else the recipe's creation slice) with trajectory.slice applied from epoch 1; wealth hold keeps the current, target interpolates linearly in f_i; events = every trajectory.events entry with week in (W_{i−1}, W_i] in given order; the app appends epochs one at a time in one group (§7.4), each folded before the next is built (a cancellable background job; completed epochs stand if stopped); a replay folds the stored epochs; the trajectory rides only as provenance on epoch 1.

Growing from a founding (3.3.3): at creation T1's card may set 'start small': the document is created at the founding population (default the lowest registered ladder's floor — 1 500 with the town product alone, a hamlet's with V07's) under the same recipe, and an advance with a target trajectory to the requested population over the requested span (default 200 years at 52-week cadence) follows as its first group; the result is a history, not the one-click town at that size (J-V6.4); both offered.

Standalone timeline (3.3.4): a Recipe.circumstances entry (§7.7) whose week lies beyond the document's week is shown on the timeline bar as a proposal; 'bring the town to this date' appends the epochs a points trajectory through the entries gives, each entry's slice and events applied at its week. Wealth over time (3.3.5): EpochInputs.wealthLevel (BCR-V6-9), when present and differing from the level in force by more than dial.hysteresis (0.05, §4.11), replaces it: layer 1's expansion rows (§7.7 item 1) re-map field.characterOffset and the granularity bonus before S6 re-evaluates drivers; item 71's class mix reads it for every placement of the epoch; absent, the level in force holds.

Sunlight over time (item 102 (b), (e)): at an epoch the buildings cast shade too, frozen in a stored mask until the next epoch. (1) When: first act of the field phase before S6 re-evaluates drivers; reads buildings as they stand after this epoch's hazards (a quarter a fire opened is sunnier at once, J-V6.29) and before any building later phases place (no loop; item 102 (c)'s one pass).

(2) Casters: every live building with its heights at the epoch's week (heightsAt for one under Works, §4.11 Works (8); stored heights otherwise), rasterised per wing (prism and roof rise, V02 §3.14.1) by existence: generated, built, altered, converted, abandoned at full ridge; decayed at the eave (roofless); ruined at shade.ruinShare (0.5) of the eave; cleared and reused none; walls, towers, castle, islands, raised ways and retaining walls are the base's casters (item 102's list, extended for item 110), not repeated.

(3) Raster: casters rasterised at shade.rasterM (4 m) as a caster-top raster: each wing's top = its own datum baseCm (V02's deriveBase stacking, BCR-V2-32: a massing tier on the tier below, a deck building on its deck, a terrace house on its platform) plus its height (max over a cell's covering wing footprints, centre rule), so each tier of a stepped building casts its own shadow (item 110 (c)); the receiver's ground(p) is the terrain raster as the field reads it — unlevelled heights (C5-54 (1)); levelled platforms enter only through buildings' datums.

(4) Sampler and reach: the base sampler's points per 32 m cell and sun positions (item 102 (a): path sun at the settlement's latitude at equinox, latitude from the realm block, DR-V8.1); per point p and sun s (azimuth α_s, elevation β_s) march toward the sun in steps of shade.rasterM: shaded when a step q at distance d has casterTop(q) > ground(p) + d · tan β_s (dmath) and d ≤ min(cot β_s, c) × h(q), h(q) = casterTop(q) − ground(q), c the sampler's cap (8; BCR-V5-15 (i), V5 §3.19 (1)) read from the sampler — one reach law for every caster (C5-31; ST-46: no absolute cap, a 90 m spire at the lowest sample reaches 720 m).

(5) Incremental and exact: the previous mask is kept; only cells whose points lie within reach downsun of a dirty caster are recomputed; dirty = (a) every building whose existence or stored heights an event changed since the previous mask's epoch (lifecycle block by seq) plus (b) every building whose Works was live at the previous mask's week or this epoch's week (C6-12), each swept by min(cot β_s, c) × h at the larger of its two heights; incremental equals full bit for bit (T-V6-12); a mask whose sampler digest differs reads as zero building shade until the next epoch recomputes it whole (dry run: 'the buildings' shade returns at the next year').

(6) Into the field: §4.5's daylight driver reads per point and sun the union of the base casters' shading and the mask's bit; shade(x) the shaded share, driver −w_sun · shade(x) (item 102 (a)); the prosperity brush still overrides; w_sun = 0 makes the mask inert (T-V6-12 no-op). (7) The drift: S6's re-banding past the hysteresis marks due blocks, so a quarter walled in by tall new houses or put in an island's shade changes field band at the first epoch after the mask records the casters, then drifts only through the wealth ladder (rung 1 at that due epoch, rung 2 after the ladder table's years); sunlit quarters drift up likewise (item 102 (e)); item 102 (d)'s sunlit-side preference acts at every placement an epoch makes.

(8) Islands: (a) as casters, an island's strip is V05's from its persisted shadeBasis, written by each epoch's S6 from the island as it stands at the epoch's start — the same one-epoch lag, surviving save and load (C5-01); (b) as receivers, the mask runs on each island arena's own 32 m lattice with that island's buildings as casters, OR-ed into V05's shadeSky (C5-32); an island raised this epoch (sky.islands, after the field phase) or declared since the last field phase has no mask on its lattice until the next field phase; absent = zero building shade (J-V5.72; TR-16).

(9) Way surfaces (V1-3.7.3's epoch clause; V11 row 90's S6 reader; SCC-95; J-V6.121): last act of the field phase in its batch after S6's re-banding: candidates = ways fronted by a plot whose fieldBand S6 changed this epoch (never a scan of every way), way-address order; each candidate without an edited surface takes V01's way-surface rule again (way.surface row for its class, era row, fronting blocks' band by V1-3.7.3's area-weighted reading); a plot's band moves only past §4.5's hysteresis so surfaces never flicker; where the value differs one setAttr of Way.surface (author engine, cause rule:field); raised roads and aqueducts never candidates; edited surfaces kept and reported (shade.surfacesHeld); draws nothing; in the epoch's undo record; renderer (V1-5.1.2) and exports read the new value from the epoch's DisplayDelta; a way bounding two districts re-laid once; report shade.surfacesRelaid.

Departure matching (step (c) first half): when the target lies below the manifest the roster's suffix leaves in reverse ordinal order (§4.11) — WHO; WHERE is the exposure field's (item 8 (c)): (1) per band b poorest first, L_b the leavers, n_b = count(L_b); (2) candidates D_b = occupied buildings housing a band-b household less the protected, each keyed k = u^(1/w) with w = E(x) · rate(building) at its centroid and u its first draw on stream(EVO_DEPARTURES, building) (dmath pow; weighted draw without replacement, largest keys first; E = 0 sorts last by address); (3) dwellings taken in descending key until their band-b households number ≥ n_b, the last may keep some (a relet down), every other empties.

(4) Swap: a household of an emptying dwelling not in L_b moves into a slot an L_b member frees in a non-emptying dwelling (pairs in address order of movers and freed slots; destination the mover's district first, then the town, §4.7 overflow order), each a relocate lifecycle event; a leaving household in a protected building leaves and its slot is refilled from an emptying dwelling of its band, so a protected building stays occupied; with no emptying dwelling to refill from the household still leaves and the protected building keeps one household fewer (a relet down, never a vacate of its last household by this step), counted uses.heldByProtection (C6-30). (5) Ops: relet down or vacate at the last; a dossier-backed use in an emptying building relocated first; departures take no churn cap (item 8 (f)); the lottery strikes fabric only (BCR-V6-23 to §4.11 step (c)).

Strike candidates (step (c) second half): the base's lottery runs once per district over one pool of three layers' candidates (persistence rates set the shares, §4.11's table); weight w = E(x) · rate(layer) · u, u the first draw on stream(EVO_DECLINE, entity) for the epoch; strikes taken in descending w, ties by address, no second draw, until the district's fabric churn cap or the 2-plots-per-block bound stops it (C6-30).

Building candidates (rate 0.6): an abandoned building whose decay Works has run (→ decay toward ruined, §4.11 Works (5)); a decayed one whose decay Works has run (→ ruin); a ruined building with salvage demand in its haul radius (→ robStone for masonry, clear otherwise), weight × min(1, demand ÷ yield) — with no demand never a candidate, so a ruin beyond any building stands.

Plot-boundary candidates (rate 0.3): a plot whose every building is cleared or reused (or none), not an informal plot with structures, empty for its drawn plots.mergeAfterYears (on stream(EVO_DECLINE, plot) keyed with the epoch it emptied, re-drawn not stored); a struck plot is amalgamated into an occupied block neighbour sharing a boundary that carries no RetainingWall (item 110 (a)) with amalgamateWeight 0.6 vs plotToGarden 0.4 on its second draw (longest shared boundary, ties by address), or with no such neighbour plotToGarden (keeping any retaining wall: a terraced garden), kind by area (< 400 m² garden, < 2 000 m² orchard, else field); plus at the same rate a cleared rear building on a lived plot (cleared for its drawn span while the front is lived in → reuse as garden, trace joined to the yard, §4.9; C6-31) and a passage whose served rear plots have all been vacant for their drawn span (→ sealPassage, §4.11; regrowth reopens it first).

Street candidates (rate 0.08): a way of streets.classes every fronting plot of which has been empty, garden, orchard or field for streets.abandonAfterYears, carrying no live plot's only access edge (§4.7's access test), neither locked nor pinned (→ downgradeWay to path; a track to path too); the line persists; regrowth upgrades it back before cutting a new lane.

Product rows (ST-26): at an epoch whose product declares rows (V07's village) the pool reads them: a building's rate × persistence[class] of its live or last use (V07's church × 0.3, manor × 0.5); the street candidate takes street.classes and issues street.op (V07's retireWay → abandoned, BCR-V7-32, ST-27); with op retireWay the test is stricter (TR-03; J-V6.107): no entry, approach or landing (V07 §3.12's disuse test) and its retirement leaves no gate, frame exit or occupied plot without a path over ways still in use (§5.3's network invariant on the network less that way), filtered before the draw; struck again: with again declared, an abandoned hollow way is a candidate at the same rate once its dwell band has run (the first band of §4.11's decline table, vacant → derelict, [10, 30] years, drawn once on stream(EVO_DECLINE, way) keyed with the retirement epoch) → effaceWay → decayed, never a candidate again; reopen issued by regrowth tier (5′) and the placement rule before any placement on a plot a retired way serves (TT-01, TU-05).

Item 110's pool kinds (V6 §3.19): raised (rate 0.05) — spans of a disused raised way (breach) and their rubble and freed supports (dismantle, on salvage demand only); retaining (rate 0.05) — a stretch of a generated retaining wall under abandoned terraces; deck (rate 0.08, the street's) — a deck whose crossing is dead and which carries no occupied plot; rates are BCR-V6-26's persistence rows.

Landfall candidates (rate 0.08; ST-13; J-V6.99): members of a fallen_island decoration (V5 §3.16 (4)-(5)): covered ways, retaining walls, plots, reservations; weight w × min(1, demand ÷ yield) of the salvage ledger's demand in the haul radius (the landfall's rubble credited, V5 §3.16 (6)), no demand → never a candidate; charged to the member district's fabric cap; a struck way takes back class and surface by a setAttr pair (cause rule:landfall): class to its formerClass (cleared) and surface re-laid by the base's surface rule for that class at its district's band (absent formerClass → class stays track, surface re-laid, reported landfallClassUnknown); a struck retaining-wall member restored by V6 §3.19.4 (6); a struck plot or reservation leaves the decoration, its ruin treatment ending (regrowth tier (3) may build); the quarry face steps to commons by retypeLand after land.scrubAfterYears (drawn once keyed with the fall's epoch) once the ledger's credit from it is spent.

Every member leaves by the op that ends its cover (TR-05; J-V6.108): a setAttr of members in that op's batch removing it in its DecorationMember form (Id, {raised, span}, {raised, support} on item 244's keys, kept by a re-derivation): way, plot or reservation when this kind strikes it; retaining-wall in the batch of the repairRetaining restoring its covered stretches; land-use in the batch whose retypeLand steps its quarry face to commons; raised span or support in the batch of repairRaised (a span's repair restores the ruined supports at its ends) or dismantle; a member tombstoned by any other op (hand delete, re-cut, clearing under a new raised way) in that op's batch; the decoration tombstoned (cause rule:landfall) in the batch removing its last member; a never-repaired never-salvaged raised part stays a member and the decoration stands.

Accesses under the rubble (TR-06; V4 §3.10 Access closures): in the batch in which a member leaves, every AccessPoint V4 §3.10 bricked with cause convert:fallIsland whose ground host is that member takes a setAttr of state back to open (locked where knownTo secret), cause rule:landfall; the member's face enters EpochScope.surfaceChanged so under.access re-derives the excavation reading and openings over it in the same epoch (V6 §3.18.1 (2d)); a lived void whose only access this was is accessible again; counted in the report's landfall section, chronicled landfallCleared ('{year}: the rubble of {subject} is cleared from {district}.'); V05 §3.16 (4) cites this as the clearance.

Not in the pool: enceinte walls (their pathway is §3.7's), the underground (under.fade runs after the pool at this step), terrain and water (V6 §3.12); candidates beyond a cap wait in key order, first in line next epoch (§4.11 Churn).

Hinterland over epochs (item 26): a struck farmstead's fields stay worked, owner passing to the nearest farmstead or commons; a plotToGarden on the town's edge in the hinterland pseudo-district joins the adjacent same-kind LandUse face; fields follow the food demand (S2's farm households and food) against the hinterland unit's worked area per household: (1) decline — the fallow ladder: when worked arable exceeds demand by more than dial.hysteresis (0.05), surplus faces (farthest from any live farmstead first by way-graph distance, ties by address; never locked, pinned or dossier-listed) step down one rung when their drawn span has run (with V07's rows: slack 20 %, order perimeterPoorest, cap one great field per epoch): arable or strip_field → pasture after land.fallowAfterYears, pasture → commons after land.scrubAfterYears, commons → wildwood after land.woodAfterYears (each drawn once on stream(EVO_DECLINE, landUse) keyed with the epoch it entered its kind), each a retypeLand charged to the hinterland pseudo-district's fabric cap; meadows, orchards, vineyards, coppice, quarries, mines, fisheries not on the ladder.

(2) Growth — the re-take: when demand exceeds the worked area, pasture → arable then commons → arable (nearest a farmstead first), each a retypeLand, and only then S12a sites new fields on new ground; wildwood cleared only by S12a's own rows (an assart), never by the re-take. (3) Farmsteads follow §3.5.1-§3.5.2; a leaving farm household empties its farmstead, whose fields enter the ladder.

Growth (1) residual, crowding hook, backlog: R₀ = delta-demand households no tier (0)-(5″) placed plus any pool household those tiers could not place; the underground crowding hook first (base order (6); II.7.3 (c)): crowdingShare (II.7.4's row) of R₀'s poorest-band households (rounded half up) offered underground — S7b (6)'s underground allocation and U-FRONT (V04 §3.4, §3.10) seat them on lived runs, then reopened runs (only where Features.sewers is on), then accessible void clusters (at any rung of the base product whether or not sewers; ST-19; BCR-V6-28, TR-09) only (V04's excavation reading accessible, item 109 (j) (4)); the seated leave R₀ (J-V6.67); R = the rest; B = the overflow backlog (households the overflow ladder housed earlier and still houses: informal plots and tents with tenure cause rule:overflow, and those crowded above ⌈band row × crowdFactor⌉), derived never stored; H = households after departures; q = min(quantumShare × H, quantumHouseholds); C = Σ max(0, households − band row) over crowding-band dwellings (derived).
