Growth (2) decision (no draw), in order: the rich build outside — R_rich = R's households of a band above crowdBands; when > 0 a stage grows for R_rich only (plots at their band's area, ribbon along the arterial whose frontage carries the highest field value outside the last boundary; J-V6.17); a stage for demand and backlog — when R + B ≥ q, a stage for R + B, the backlog relocating into it (tents, informal plots, then over-crowded; tent clusters and emptied informal plots cleared by the decline ladder as vacant; whatever the cadence, C6-10); overflow — when 0 < R and R + B < q, the overflow ladder rung by rung until every household is housed (none dropped, §5.2 F-PLAN): (i) crowding past crowdFactor up to §2.6's capacity poorest first, (ii) informal tenure on vacant, cleared or ruined plots of the lowest-value district (item 70 clusters, a build Works of days, tenure cause rule:overflow), (iii) a tent cluster (item 70 tents) on the edge belt of overflow.tentBeltM outside the outermost boundary along the busiest arterial — never fails; they are next epochs' backlog B, first in line for tiers (0)-(5); decrowding — else when C ≥ max(q, crowdShareMax × H) a stage for the crowded excess (households above band row in descending ordinal relocate; BCR-V6-18); else no stage.

Growth (3) regime: the wall decision (V6 §3.7.1) first; a walled stage takes the walled-ring regime; otherwise ribbon (anisotropy 4) below ribbonMaxHouseholds (150), suburb (3) otherwise (§4.4 regime rows; BCR-V6-19 admits suburb for a history epoch's unwalled stage beside preset, era row, shanty toggle); FTG's configured suburb stage (research/findings/ftg-docs-params.md §1.4, §2.7) the emulation reference (J-V6.18); the rich-residual stage always ribbon. (4) The stage: §4.11's grow path from S5 (S5a boundary grown for the stage's households, S5b gate law, S5c built-face legality, S5d) then S6-S13 on the new faces (S7b (1)'s district supply term with old districts' standing members as providers, item 105 (g)); afterGrowth participants on the new faces only; a new stage's S5b may take a viaduct from the base's raised-way solver in the same epoch reading the same RaisedWayLedger (BCR-V6-25); its S10 and S11 level terraced faces with retaining walls and cut deck faces; land never shrinks the frame. (5) Crowding is siting tier (5″): crowding-band households relet up dwelling by dwelling to ⌈band row × crowdFactor⌉, never above §2.6's capacity, while C stays below crowdShareMax × H; the rich do not crowd.

A new circuit (evaluated once when growth grows a stage; on a dossier-bound document only when the dossier gate admits one, V6 §3.7.6 (4)): all hold — threat ≥ walls.threatMin (slice; DR2); share of households outside the outermost enceinte (new stage counted) ≥ extramuralShareMin; household-weighted mean prosperity ≥ prosperityMin; youngest enceinte's creation ≥ minIntervalYears ago (or none); the era row admits walls (S0's walls toggle rows); then fires when u < 1 − (1 − chancePerYear × eraFactor)^years, u the first draw on stream(EVO_GROWTH, town root); the creation event records the four conditions' values as why rows (BCR-V6-20), read by the enceinte provider.

A circuit makes the new stage a walled ring with placement aroundAll enclosing every earlier stage on its approachable arcs (item 106 (a): barrier arcs close it and are not walled), absorbing the suburbs between (S5a's trace by the registered EnceinteStrategy, S7's furniture); the stage's land widened on walled arcs only so the inner strip lies wholly on new land (t_k raised until the lattice distance from every footprint to the boundary ≥ strip width + ringBlockM 40 m); barrier arcs keep the stage's boundary (never pushed into the sea or over a cliff); absorbed districts' extramural false, the character step re-types kinds past item 72's hysteresis, the exposure field drops the extramural term from the next epoch; the old outermost ring enters its pathway (superseded); F-WALL's ladder (§5.2) binds the trace; a failed trace leaves the stage unwalled, re-evaluated at the next growth (reported).

Pathway of a superseded ring: at supersession neglect (existence abandoned), Enceinte.supersededBy set, pathway {since, cause superseded, fate (keep while threat ≥ keepThreat, else drawn from fateWeights road 0.7 absorb 0.3 on stream(EVO_FORT, enceinte)), eligibleWeek = since + round(52 × y), y uniform in roadAfterYears [30, 80] or absorbAfterYears [20, 60]}; a keep re-drawn once the first epoch its threat falls below keepThreat; each epoch the fortification phase, for every ring with a pathway not locked (address order): (1) gates open from their drawn gateOpenAfterYears at gateOpenChancePerYear (0.15) → gateToJunction, a square when ≥ 3 primaries meet (a gate market).

(2) Stretches dismantled: the trace cut into dismantleStretchM stretches from its first tower in address order; each not yet dismantled (its condition run not dismantled) at dismantleChancePerYear × min(1, 0.2 + demand ÷ yield) (our own floor 0.2) → dismantle with the stretch (condition → dismantled, f item 575; TT-04), crediting the ledger (§4.11 Salvage), charged to the fabric cap of the stretch midpoint's district; a stretch holding a raised gate whose deck stands is no candidate (filtered before the draw) until that raised way is removed or its crossing span dismantled (V6 §3.7.6 (5); TU-01 (d)).

(3) The end: from eligibleWeek with threat < keepThreat: road → wallToWay (§4.11; its dossier-backed uses relocated first); absorb → absorbWall (wall role rows removed; strips' setback and glacis lines removed so strips merge into blocks; S10's incremental re-cut cuts plots on freed land with neighbours fixed (§4.7 S10 (7)), writing plot_line rows where plots meet the old line; existence cleared (cause convert:absorbWall), name kept; remaining runs keep condition with towers and gates, dismantling continues on the cleared record until every run is dismantled but a stretch holding a raised gate under a standing deck; a tower or gate is never a pool candidate; J-V6.112); neither fires on an innermost enceinte of a castle or citadel (kind citadel or bailey), which keeps its keep fate; the ring road named by S13a with formerWall; an absorbed wall draws no label, its record read by the enceinte provider ('the old wall ran along these plot backs until year N').

Outermost ring in long safety: an outermost unsuperseded ring whose threat ≤ walls.neglectThreatMax has held for neglectAfterYears (read from the epochs' slices, counted from the later of the low threat's start and the ring's last lifted neglect; TU-02) enters its pathway (cause neglected, fate keep): neglect at once; gates open as §3.7.2 (1); stretches breached (each a breached run of condition, f item 575) at walls.breachChancePerYear in the decline pool's fabric cap (base rate wall 0.05 as weight factor); no final conversion (only supersession or a hand edit makes a road of it; J-V6.13).

A shorter ring (item 8 (a); under item 106's closure and water rule): an enceinte whose intramural occupied-plot share has stayed below contract.occupiedShareMax since underuseSince for contract.afterYears while threat ≥ contract.threatMin contracts at contract.chancePerYear (first draw on stream(EVO_FORT, enceinte) after the pathway draws). Trace: (1) region = the T-level set (§4.4) inside the ring holding coreShare of its households; while harbour use is live, united with its quay frontage (live quays, landings, basin edges, water gates) and the shortest way-graph path from core to it; plus marginM (40 m); (2) line = the EnceinteStrategy tracing the region's boundary under barrier closure (approachable arcs walled, ends anchored with a tower) on the S3 lattice with the built-face legality cost field: occupied footprint impassable, vacant/ruined/cleared footprint or plot boundary or back lane low rate, way corridor middle rate.

(3) Strips clear only vacant, ruined or cleared buildings (demolish, cause convert:contractWall); a strip reaching an occupied one, or a trace leaving a live quay unreachable through a gate or open front, widens the margin by 20 m and retraces, at most three times; then the contraction waits for the next epoch, reported (walls.waited; never forced). (4) contractWall (§4.11) builds the new ring with gates where primaries cross (S5a, S7); the old ring takes pathway {cause contracted, fate keep} and decays by §3.7.3's breach and §3.7.2 (2)'s dismantling; plots between the two rings are extramural from then on.

Renewed threat: a ring with pathway cause neglected or contracted whose threat rises back to walls.threatMin is repaired: repairWall on each breached run in chain order from the trace's first vertex, each at its effective week with no Works (J-V6.31, J-V6.90), towers and gates standing again with it (TU-01), fabric cap charged (runs beyond wait in chain order); pathway cleared when no run is breached, lifecycle returning to its former state when every run is standing; in the batch clearing the pathway (also when no run was breached) a no-stretch repairWall (cause rule:threat) lifts the ring's unlifted neglect (in use when every run standing, decayed while a dismantled run remains) — a ring whose pathway is cleared is never abandoned; a contracted ring never neglected takes none (TU-02; J-V6.115); counted walls.backInUse, chronicled wallManned; a dismantled run is not rebuilt (a hand repairWall on it bends to drawWall; ST-35).

A ring in use with a breach (TT-05; J-V6.110): a ring with no pathway whose condition holds a breached run while threat > neglectThreatMax (a landfall's breach, V5 §3.16 (4), or a hand breach) is repaired at the next fortification phase by the same op and order (repairWall per breached run, no Works, towers and gates standing again with the run, fabric cap, runs beyond wait); a dismantled run stays a gap (J-V6.16); a locked or pinned ring held; a ring in use at or below neglectThreatMax is not repaired by this rule (its threat's rise repairs it; long safety enters §3.7.3); counted walls.repairedInUse.

Barriers, water and the dossier's walls (item 106; C6-07) bind every trace (circuit, shorter ring, repaired or re-anchored stretch): (1) barrier closure on every trace under item 106 (arcs classified by V11's walls.barriers rows, V11 §3.16: sheer cliff or deep water closes; steep slope or deep marsh closes behind a light wall; open ground the full curtain; only approachable arcs walled; ends anchored with a tower; a river loop or spur walled across its neck; a barrier within wall.barrierReachM beyond the boundary may be reached, spare ground intramural gardens (106 (b)); stretch profile grades the curtain (106 (c)); aroundAll = encloses every earlier stage on approachable arcs.

(2) Water access is a hard rule on every new ring and contraction: every live quay, landing, harbour basin and water gate stays reachable from inside through a gate or open front; a circuit that would cut one off gains a water gate on the arc between quay and water (S7) or, on a barrier arc, leaves it open; a contraction takes the harbour into its region; a trace that cannot hold both this and the occupied-footprint rule retraces by the margin rule and then waits, reported, never forced (J-V6.58).

(3) The waterfront at each epoch (item 106 (d)-(f)): the fortification phase re-reads the waterfront grade from DR2's sea threats by V11's walls.waterfront rows (highest-weight applying row) past dial.hysteresis: a rise to a quay_wall row on a walled port turns open into quay_wall with sea gates at the row's quay accesses (drawWall on the waterfront arc, cause rule:waterfront, fabric cap, no Works, chronicled waterfront); a threat below every quay-wall row for neglectAfterYears neglects the quay wall (pathway neglected, keep), never demolished; a walled port without a harbour-mouth chain gains one the first epoch its mouth is enclosed (two towers on mole/breakwater heads or shores and a water gate, S7; chronicled harbourChain), a tower or fort already at a mole head (item 110 (d)'s landmark) is the chain's anchor there (C6-53).

(3) cont.: a removal holds (C6-38 (7)): a generated quay wall or harbour-mouth chain the user deletes carries detail.suppress (BCR-V6-24; key the enceinte and the waterfront's water body, or the enceinte and the harbour basin); never re-added while live (condition still holding reported walls.suppressedHeld); undo lifts; the user's re-add (drawWall on the former line, placeGate at the former mouth) serves it while it stands (V6 §3.19.3 (7); SR3-08); a reclaim or shiftCourse of the previous epoch changing a shoreline an enceinte's closure relies on re-evaluates that closure by least disruption (item 22): a barrier arc turned approachable gets a new stretch anchored on the old ones; a stretch no longer needed is neglected, never demolished.

(4) The dossier gate (item 20 through DR2; J-V6.59): on a dossier-bound document the engine never adds an enceinte or waterfront wall the dossier's walls records do not admit: §3.7.1's circuit decision runs only when the records admit one more enceinte than stands (by record kind — palisade, town walls, city walls and gates — against the rung's ring rows), and then without the chance draw; a walls REPLACEMENT step (item 108) or a new walls record at dossier triggers the circuit at this epoch's growth phase with the record's kind — around the residual's stage if there is one, else around the present built boundary through the hand drawWall operator's path (cause the dossier event; no face added) — and the superseded ring enters its pathway; waterfront grade follows (3); contraction, neglect, breach and dismantling stay map facts (records list walls, not their line).

(5) Raised ways on every trace (item 110 (b); C6-46; J-V6.91): a raised way's support footprint is a footprint for §3.7.1's strip rule and impassable in §3.7.4 (2)'s cost field (never demolished for a wall); a trace crosses a raised way only under a span over land, never through a support or along its under-deck strip; the crossing is S7 furniture: an aqueduct a wall opening (an arch, not a gate; V1C-68 (6)), a viaduct or elevated road a raised gate at deck level (its portal on the raised part only; the part-0 way beneath takes its own ground gate by S5a's law); continuity is a hard rule (a trace unable to cross under a span retraces by the margin rule then waits, reported walls.waited, never forced); absorbWall and wallToWay leave standing every raised way crossing the old line (the ring road takes no junction; the opening or raised gate stays free-standing); dismantling never takes a stretch holding a raised gate whose deck stands (taken from the first epoch after that way is removed or its crossing span dismantled); a wall opening under an aqueduct is no support and goes with its stretch (TU-01 (d); J-V6.114).

Displaced pool first: households a hazard, a contraction's strip, a Works, a clearance, a sealed void (cause void) or the island step (cause island; BCR-V5-23) displaced this epoch are in the ledger's pool; siting places them first through the same tiers (addresses kept; each a relocate clearing transit; any unplaced join the growth phase's R₀ so a stage or the overflow ladder houses them within the epoch), then the delta demand less the households taken by demandTaken, band by band.

Regrowth tiers (§4.11 (0)-(6)), candidates ranked by §4.7 S10b's score for the household's band (descending), ties by address: (0) relet up in standing shells below their band row; (1) reoccupy vacant buildings (builtBand = household band first), leaving vacant decline.turnoverVacancy of each band's dwellings (poorest 5 %, others 1 %, 0 in parity presets; the most exposed first by E(x)) (FTG's poorest pools, research/findings/ftg-docs-params.md §3.3; C6-34); a vacant building whose rear plots a sealed passage served taken only after openPassage reopens it; (2) reoccupy derelict ones (a repair, a ledger debit); (3) rebuild or reuse … build on ruins, burned shells, cleared traces (class by S10b's mix at the plot's field band, item 71; footprint kept when the template admits, else S11; successor at the trace's address §6.3); (4) vacant plots of the old plan beyond the band's vacancy-run share (S10 (8)) — a vacant deck plot only to a use V11 §3.24.4's per-use deckOk admits (effective crypt first — class, bound dossier crypt record or cryptAlways keyword — then the class column; SCC-31).

A placement on a retired way reopens it first (TT-01, TU-05; J-V6.107): at every placement an epoch makes (siting tiers (0)-(5), the village's (6v)-(9v) (V07 §3.12), the use phase's openings and moves incl. relaxation and split shop, a dossier-backed use's relocation) on a plot whose access edge (§4.7) is a retired hollow way (abandoned or decayed set by retireWay or effaceWay) the placement is made only after reopenWay restores it in the same batch (no cap); where it reaches ways in use only through other retired ways, every retired way on its shortest way-graph path (by length, ties by address) is reopened with it (§5.3); a locked or pinned retired way is never reopened by the engine — a plot needing one is no candidate at any tier, in the use phase or for a relocation; reopenings counted with tier (5′)'s (ways.reopened).

(5′) upgrade of downgraded ways and reopening of retired ones (TR-03): before tier (5) cuts a plot on a face a downgradeWay'd lane or retired hollow way bounds, upgradeWay or the rows' reopen restores it (the old lane back before a new one is cut) at every rung under whichever product's siting runs; reopenWay (→ built, class kept; BCR-V7-32) under any product, keyed to the way's own ladder, so hollow ways of a village handed up are reopened by the town's regrowth (J-V6.107); no cap (item 8 (f)); (5) plots S10 cuts on faces the old plan left unbuilt along its street lines inside the last boundary — deck faces among them (a mole, pier, quay platform or bridge deck in use holding no plot; cut by S10's deck rule within the deck's width under V11 §3.24.4's deck table as V2 §3.16 reads it; buildings only for deckOk uses; a suppressed deck slot skipped and counted held, ST-15, ST-51); (5″) crowding (V6 §3.6 (5)); (6) new faces — the growth phase with the underground crowding hook first (accessible capacity only; BCR-V6-28); tiers (5′) and (5″) are this strategy's own between the base's (5) and (6) (BCR-V6-18).

Informal clusters in decline: a vacant, cleared or ruined plot of a district whose value fell past the hysteresis at the epoch takes tenure informal (§4.11 Informal clusters over epochs) only when the overflow ladder or the poorest band's delta demand needs it — never a cluster without households.

Ladder schedule (step (d)): due blocks in address order; per block the base's rungs (§4.11 Survivors) 1, 2, 3, each charged to its cap kind (geometry for rung 3's re-cuts and rebuilds, fabric for rung 1's infill); a block exhausting its per-block maximum waits; rung-3 triggers the engine supplies: vacancy (emptied plots), ruin (the lottery's), a destructive event (burn, topple, flood collapses: struck plots eligible from the event's epoch), redevelopment (the base's composite on a due block growing rich only where rung 3's years in the band have run and relocations fit the use cap); after the rungs, due MutationPlan steps; on terraced and deck ground (item 110 (a), (d)): rung-3 subdivide or amalgamate keeps every RetainingWall as a fixed plot line and refuses an amalgamate across one; on a deck plot no rung-2 densify (no yard, no back_court), a relet within the deck building's capacity, MutationPlan steps and rebuilds through S11's capped mutator (V2 §3.16 (3)), a rung-3 re-cut keeps deck plots inside the deck's width.

The uses phase runs once per epoch after the field and the island participant on the households standing at the epoch's start; departures come later (base order), so a use's catchment is judged with a one-epoch lag absorbed by the strain memory (J-V6.8); it is §4.11's use step (1)-(6) with V6's order, counts, memory and records.

Counts (items 20, 108): for every roster class c with a use, N_c = its manifest count at the epoch's target; (1) no dossier record covers c: D_c = live dossier-backed single uses (never closed here), L_c = other live uses; surplus = max(0, L_c − max(0, N_c − D_c)), deficit = max(0, N_c − D_c − L_c) (the roster fills only what the dossier does not list, item 20 (h)).

(2) A dossier collective record R (COUNT, QUARTER or GUILD) covers c (by V11's dossier.ladders, V11 §3.12; item 108 (a)): R owns c's members (108 (c)); member target M_R = clamp(perCapita_c(target), R.range) — S2's per-capita count at the target clamped into the record's numeric range, else V11 §3.12's rung rule range (at a village rung V07 §2.4's row, J-V7.105; SCC-33, SCC-64, TT-06); the generator owns no use of c (L_c = 0); a standing generator use of c is re-bound to R (assign to R's next free member key #k, J-A74.73, no move, cause rule:ladder, no cap, counted uses.ladderRebound); surplus = max(0, count(members(R)) − M_R), deficit = max(0, M_R − count(members(R))); members above M_R close by 3.9.4's order under J-V6.24's cap, below open by 3.9.6 as R's next keys; never closes members #1 … #min(R.range) nor a member the dossier names individually; several records covering one class share it by the base's rule (QUARTER's district holds its raised share, item 72; COUNT owns the rest; counted once; T-V6-45); e.g. 'Blacksmiths (3-10)' tracks S2's per-capita row, never < 3 nor > 10, no generator smithy beside them (J-V6.57).

Strain (Use.strain, BCR-V6-4): per live use in address order: demand ratio ρ = H(u) ÷ h_c by nearest-provider catchments (item 107 (c)): one labelled multi-source Dijkstra per class per epoch over the way graph (§12.6 cost unit), sources the class's live uses labelled, bounded at serviceRadiusM; H(u) = households labelled u; h_c = town households ÷ N_c; N_c = 0 → ρ = 0; a split pair's shop is the class's provider, its works none; supply: a hard SupplyEdge of c whose resource has no live provider (producing-class use, resource site, chain node, import store) within its maxDistanceM by its mode; strain set {kind, sinceWeek} when ρ < closeShare (demand) or supply fails (supply) and none present; kind updated (sinceWeek kept) when the other takes over; cleared when neither; each write a setAttr on Use.strain (author engine) with the epoch's undo; a user can clear it by hand ('give this shop time').

Closing a failing use: a use neither dossier-backed nor pinned closes (closeUse, leave vacant, cause strain) when its strain has lasted closeAfterYears (demand) or starveAfterYears (supply) ((week − sinceWeek) ÷ 52 against the class row; BCR-V6-4 reads these in years); no cap; the building stays vacant (decline ladder's first rung), its former use in formerUses (§4.11 (5)); a live-in owner household stays; a split pair is one institution (strain = the shop's demand and the works' supply; closing closes both in one op).

Closing the surplus: when the manifest falls, surplus uses of c close (cause surplus) in uses.closeSurplusBy order: longest-strained first, then most over-served coverage unit (item 103 (f), highest served-to-target ratio), then lowest present score, then address; dossier-backed single uses, a record's protected members and pinned uses never chosen (a pinned one counted heldByPin); charged to the district's use cap (§4.11 Churn), the rest wait in that order (the lag on the way down, item 8 (f)).

Moving a thriving use: every live unpinned use not closing this epoch (dossier-backed ones included) re-scored in address order against a snapshot of scores taken at the phase's start, except a use whose bound providers or consumers a committed op changed is re-scored on the committed state (J-V6.25, J-V6.54); never moved by this rule: a church-family use whose plot holds a churchyard and a singular use (the cathedral, a see's seat, the castle's keep) — closing only by surplus, strain or the dossier; a see moves only by the dossier, its building's ruin or demolition, or a rung crossing opening or closing its class (J-V6.66).

(1) Candidates: plots of its catchment (its district and neighbouring districts united with plots within serviceRadiusM) holding a vacant building, a cleared or ruined trace or no building, not reserved, locked, pinned, informal with structures, or a dossier-listed ruin, whose building S11's compatibility table can bring to c's designation (§4.7 S11 (1)); a deck plot only when V11 §3.24.4's per-use deckOk admits the use (effective crypt first; SCC-31) so a dossier-backed use with a crypt record is never moved onto a deck; a candidate on a retired hollow way scored as any other, the winning placement reopening it first with every retired way on its path (TU-05); a candidate needing a locked or pinned retired way is none. (2) Score: the PlacementSolver's score (§4.7 S10b) summing the prosperity field (item 102's driver in it), neighbourhood character (item 72), item 103's families, signature pairs and coverage pull (cov/<class>), item 102 (d)'s sunlit preference, item 105's two-way link term under the class's orientation with item 107 (b)'s comfort plateau, item 107 (d)'s same-kind far row (spc/<class>), a custom chain's edges, and the controlled chance drawn on use.relocate (§6.1); the present plot scored the same way.

(3) Decision: the use's first draw on use.relocate for the epoch is its move-chance gate — only below 1 − (1 − moveChance)^years are candidates scored (each candidate's chance drawn after it, address order), and the best a* wins when score(a*) − score(present) > inertia (J-V6.68); the move charged to the district's use cap, refused moves waiting ordered by gain, first next epoch; a candidate an earlier mover took is skipped. (4) Op: relocateUse(use, a*) (§4.11); a differing designation → a MutationPlan spreads it over epochs; a live-in class brings its owner household (a relocate into the destination's residential slot); the vacated building keeps the former use in formerUses.

Opening what the manifest lacks: deficits open class by class in item 105 (f)'s order (anchors fixed — terrain resources and outside classes at S12a's sites, markets, gates, harbour, never opened here; then S10a's field-driving classes; then source-oriented by depth (topological over the class supply graph, a loop broken at its lowest-weight link, ties by class id); then balanced; then market-oriented, per V11 §3.7.3); each opening runs the solver town-wide over 3.9.5 (1)'s candidate set, scoring the top uses.openCandidates (64) by S10a's class raster then the full score (deck plots only where deckOk admits; a retired-way candidate's winning opening reopens the way first); coverage served counts recomputed after every committed opening and closing (items 103 (f), 107 (a)); a building whose formerUses holds c takes the class row's inertia as a bonus; a use a fire closed this epoch counts in the deficit and reopens with that bonus.

Opening details: an always-crypt class (V11's cathedral and great-temple rows) opening into an existing building admits only buildings whose basement region can hold the class's cryptM2 (V11; V6 §3.18.3 (5)), else the best-scored candidate with V03's rank trimming others (never below their vaults); each opening an openUse (cause demand, or coverage when the coverage pull is the largest contribution) with a MutationPlan when the building must change; its Use minted with the town root as derivation unit, the phase's stage id, the epoch and its ordinal in the opening order as creation index (§6.3); openings take no cap (item 8 (f)); a strain-closed use with a class deficit is replaced where the solver now scores best — a new business, not the old one moved (J-V6.23).

Claim-sized classes at a village rung (TU-04's V06 companion from V07 §3.12 (c); J-V6.119): a cloister-family class, or a market-hall-family class without a nearMarket row, opening at a village-rung epoch — a roster member in this uses step, a record through the product's records placement in the dossier step (TV-02) — takes a candidate plot only with its vacant neighbours joined by S10 (7)'s join law (V6 §3.8.4's amalgamate form, neighbours fixed, never across a retaining wall), the joins charged to the district's geometry cap for a roster member (a candidate whose joins the remaining cap cannot hold is none); a record's joins are its dossier event's disruption, charged to no churn cap, bounded by the request kind's DisruptionBudgetRow and reported over budget, never refused (§7.7 item 5; TW-05, J-V6.123) — up to V07's rules.claimArea (claimArea.cloister at its band, or the hall area A_h, V07 §3.6 (4a)); no such candidate → V07 §3.12 (c)'s outside plot on the nearest hinterland face adjoining a road beyond the perimeter (village.outsidePlot), else a roster member waits in its deficit, reported (a record never waits); a market-hall with a nearMarket row and a fair_ground are placed by V07 §3.12 (a), (b), never here.

Why rows: for every opening, move and closing the phase writes on the open, relocate or close lifecycle event detail.why — the solver's top uses.moveWhyRows contributions (row id, family, share) as its explain mode returns them (§4.7 S10b; rows V11's), a supply-web link a family link row with its good and the other end's use (item 105 (j)); model data (BCR-V6-20) surviving save, load, rebase, export; the report's UseMove rows read back from them; V10's 'why is this here' (via V6's use provider) and V09's siting panel read them — never a paraphrase.

Custom content over epochs (item 104 (e), (h) (7)): a custom institution is dossier-backed (never closed here, moved only by 3.9.5 or relocated before a step empties its building); its profile the base's pure function (104 (a)); a new revision (changed content hash) arrives as a dossier event, re-resolved and re-sited by least disruption at step (e), not here; (1) an inactive chain pulls nothing (remaining nodes keep sites, edges leave scores from the next epoch, then drift by inertia); (2) an active chain moves by its anchor: when its upstream anchor changes (a DepositSite depleted or discovered, a terrain-and-water op, a new gate facing the partner) the phase re-sites its in-town nodes in item 105 (f)'s order by the solver's dossier request within the epoch, least disruption, outside the use cap (UseMove cause chain); otherwise nodes move one at a time with the one-epoch lag; (3) toggling returns (nodes keep sites; re-activated edges only raise present scores; T-V6-14); (4) close at street scale, a quarter only by emergence (item 72's threshold via the character step) or declaration (a district-defining record, a ladder QUARTER record, an author's declaration); the engine never assigns a district to a chain; the chronicle's rename line records an emerging quarter (J-V6.56).

Use step defaults by clientele (item 103 (a); a class row stating no useRules takes its row; V11 writes none by default; SCC-45; our own, calibratable): serviceRadiusM / closeShare / closeAfterYears / starveAfterYears / inertia / moveChance per year — daily-local 400 / 0.50 / 5 / 3 / 0.15 / 0.10; town-wide 1 200 / 0.40 / 10 / 5 / 0.25 / 0.05; travellers 800 / 0.40 / 8 / 5 / 0.20 / 0.08; elite 1 500 / 0.30 / 15 / 8 / 0.35 / 0.03; clandestine 800 / 0.30 / 10 / 5 / 0.30 / 0.05; institution 2 000 / never by demand / — / 10 / 0.50 / 0.01; inertia in score units (one soft row of weight 1 fully satisfied); a concealed use relocates by these rules, its front an ordinary business (§4.11 (6)); a market's square outlives its institution.

Supply web over epochs (item 105; J-V6.54, J-V6.55): (1) links derived, never stored, re-bound after every committed openUse, closeUse or relocateUse (S10b's nearest-provider binding, 105 (a), for that class's members and the classes it supplies and is supplied by; a not-yet-visited use whose bound set changed re-scored on the committed state); when a provider closes, every former consumer is bound to its nearest live provider by the end of the epoch (T-V6-41); links pull both ends; count uses.rebound. (2) Openings in 105 (f)'s order then one relaxation pass over two-way classes any of whose uses opened or moved: at most siting.web.relaxPasses (V11 §3.7.4) passes, a move only where the gain exceeds siting.web.relaxGain and only inside its own district (placement rule included), relocateUse cause relax, use cap, drawn on use.relocate; the second pass only if the first moved something, over the uses its moves re-bound (T-V6-42); counted uses.relaxMoves.

(3) Split sites over epochs (105 (h)): a split pair is one institution (works Use + shop Use whose branchOf names the works); works scored by nuisance and input rows, shop by output and clientele rows, each moving separately; closing closes both in one op; undo restores both; split: at the first epoch an unsplit live use of a split class has a split index above its class's compiled profile.split.threshold (V11 §2.3; V11 §3.7.4's splitThreshold only the default; SCC-23, SCC-69), the shop opens on the best-scored candidate (retired way reopened first) as a branchOf use (cause split, use cap); merge: when the index falls below threshold − uses.splitHysteresis, the shop closes (cause merge), plot left vacant; a split with no threshold (splitEnabled false or the split row removed mid-history; V11 §2.10; J-V11.14; SCC-70; J-V6.113) merges at the next uses phase (cause merge, use cap, beyond waiting in address order) and none opens; an author's declared split stands; an author's merge-back declaration holds the pair merged and suppresses the split; parity presets split nothing (T-V6-43); counted uses.splits, uses.merges.

(4) The district supply term (105 (g)) read by S7b (1) wherever an epoch allocates classes to districts (siting's new-plot tiers, growth's new stage) with old districts' standing members as providers already allocated. (5) SettlementForge's activeChains at each epoch (105 (i)): a change arrives in EpochInputs.dossier (V08); at the dossier phase named processors are resolved to bound members (kind family, research/sf/mapping.md row 46) and links bound; a status change weakens or restores links by V11 §3.7.4's chainStatus weight for the chain's neutral status key (V08 §2.6's chainStatus word row; SCC-32) from the next uses phase; an entrepot chain's ends are item 104 (b)'s import and export pulls; the engine never writes activeChains (item 20). (6) Explanations: a pulling link is a why row of family link (105 (j)); an author's pinned, moved or cut link is honoured by re-binding. With the web's off form (V11 §3.7.4's named cell set = parity presets; SCC-34) an epoch is byte-identical to the history without item 105 (T-V6-44, no-op pin).

Institution ladders over epochs (item 108; J-V6.57): ladder table and step types V11's (dossier.ladders, V11 §3.12), counts 3.9.1 (2)'s; a step reaches the map as a dossier event (greater with promotedFrom or lesser with demotedFrom, J-A74.73 re-binding the key) applied by item 22's least disruption: COUNT — members re-counted at the target (an upgrade keeps the lesser's building as #1 and opens the rest at the next uses phase; a demotion keeps the member nearest its demand, highest ρ, as the single lesser and closes the rest, formerUses kept); QUARTER — the character step sets the quarter identity for the record's district (item 72 raised share), the record owning the trade's members inside and by ordinary spread outside; GUILD — one guild hall opened by S10b's dossier request, workshops re-bound by assign (no move); SIZE — the building mutated to the greater template at once (§4.7 S11 (6)), Works over weeks, no extra members; REPLACEMENT — by V08 §3.5.1 (c)'s three cases (SR6-02; J-V6.125): first case (greater's thing is the lesser's: graveyard over burial_ground, wizard_s_tower over hedge_wizard, mages_guild over wizard_s_tower, professional_city_watch over town_watch, cathedral_10_000_only over parish_church) a convert in place (a church replaced by the cathedral carries its crypt in the same event; walls via V6 §3.7.6 (4)); second case (@none or @office lesser: town watch over citizen militia, cathedral over resident priest) converts nothing, the greater placed as an added record with the lesser's key its alias; third case (pin-record lesser parish_church over wayside_shrine; building lesser not kept fish_market over fishmonger) the greater placed new by S10b's dossier request, the lesser's thing left standing unbound, keys per V08 §3.5.1 (c), after promotedFrom the record's key re-pointed to the greater and a kept pin laid with no binding row (V08 §3.5.1 (d); J-V8.114); at a village rung via V07 §3.12 item 4 (records placement first); no convert on the lesser's building or pin in the second and third cases.

A custom institution whose library subsumes names other kinds (item 104) is typed by 108 (e) (guild-like GUILD, larger same-function SIZE, default SIZE) and takes the same path; a lesser reaching the map beside its greater becomes a member of the greater's collective by assign, never an addition (108 (c)); nothing double-counted at any batch (T-V6-45).

MutationPlan creation (BCR-V6-21 in the base's epoch-spread mutation): the use phase's openings and relocations into a building of a different designation, and a hand mutate … spread 'epochs', run §4.7 S11's mutator once at the creating op (the whole MutationRecord recorded in EditBase.mutations, §4.7 S11 (5)) and create a plan splitting its parts into steps: occupy (nothing geometric; first only when the present design is compatible — applied at creation, opensAt occupy; otherwise the first geometric step is due at once and the use opens at the first step whose result is compatible: a relocating use stays open at its former site and a new opening waits unopened with its deficit counted met); for an always-crypt target (crypt 'always', J-VI.17 H34) the crypt is laid at the occupy step (V02's crypt basement re-derivation, never refuses, V02 §3.14.5, BCR-V2-28) and the basement ring is exempt from the compatibility test; adapt (converted and adapted parts, subtracted parts no added part overlaps); extend (added parts overlapping no subtracted part); rebuild (subtracted parts an added part overlaps with those added parts); empty steps dropped; due weeks = creation week + round(52 × y), y drawn once per step from mutation.stepYears on stream(EVO_MUTATION, plot) in step order, each ≥ the previous; a dossier re-designation is a host change decided at once (§4.7 S11 (6)), no plan, toward an always-crypt class laying the crypt in the same event.

Application: in the ladder phase after the rungs, every plan whose next step is due (dueWeek ≤ week) applied in address order by a mutate op carrying step {plan, step} (BCR-V6-7) applying exactly that step's parts of the stored record in S11's order (subtract, convert, adapt, add), writing done and the new expect digest; adapt and extend charged to fabric, rebuild to geometry; a refused step waits; each applied step starts its Works (§4.11 Works (6)).

Guard, re-planning, cancelling: a step applies the stored record only while the building's leaf digest equals expect (§6.2); a hand edit, a later mutation or a cancelled Works breaks it and the plan is re-planned (S11's mutator from the present design to the target inside this epoch's event, record replacing the remaining steps, due weeks kept, reported replanned); cancelled (tombstoned, done steps standing) when its use leaves the building, its plot is re-derived, or a lock covers the building; a user deletes one by delete on the plan (V6 §4.2); the last step tombstones it (cause done); going back (item 18 (e)): when a building whose plan was cancelled with done steps next takes its former designation, the mutator's record is the inverse of the done steps (added subtracted, subtracted restored from the done events' records, converted converted back), spread by a new plan — never a fresh design.

Where hazards come from: (a) circumstance events whose kind names a HazardRow (standalone timeline, advance's events) and, dossier-bound, calamity records (kind calamity) typed by V6's calamity table (row's hazard, place at the F5 targets' centroid, maxBuildings or topple count or flood depth factor by severity); params override the row; params.x, params.y (metres in the document frame) give the place; params.week in (prevWeek, week], outside clamped and reported; a calamity's targets are struck in place (their uses exempt from relocation, closing as ruined where they stand, households into the ledger; the dossier phase's F5 then finds the building already struck — idempotent). (b) Spontaneous hazards only when evolution.hazards admits the row's mode; dossier-bound the mode is none by rule (adjust refused with R2's line 'this town's disasters come from its campaign'; J-V6.19); count per epoch ⌊λ⌋ plus one when a draw < λ − ⌊λ⌋, λ = rate × years (fire × live buildings ÷ 1 000), drawn first on stream(EVO_HAZARD, town root); each hazard's week uniform in the span unless given; hazards run in week order, then row order.

Fire (burn) defaults (our own; ignition calibratable §13.9): ignitionPerYearPer1000 0.2, jumpM 6, breakM 8, pCatch 0.55, flammability (lower of roof and wall: thatch or reed 1.0; timber, shingle or wattle 0.9; tile 0.45; stone, slate or brick 0.15), windDown 1.3, windUp 0.6, maxBuildings 6 under minor, 400 under full (an event may set its own). (1) Ignition at (x, y) (the building there, else nearest within 30 m), else drawn without replacement over live occupied buildings weighted flammability × (1 + block building coverage) × (2 when an item 103 EMITS fire-risk class stands within 30 m) on the town-root stream.

(2) Fire spread breadth-first in rings, each ring's candidates in address order: adjacent when footprints within jumpM and the segment between nearest points crosses no way corridor ≥ breakM wide and no water face — the part over a deck counts as land and the deck's carriageway is a way corridor, so bridge houses burn in turn while a carriageway ≥ breakM or a stone bridgehead stops it (C6-48); a neighbour catches when its draw on stream(EVO_HAZARD, neighbour) < pCatch × flammability × wind (windDown within 60° of the prevailing wind from the burning building, windUp beyond 120°, else 1); stops when a ring adds nothing or the burnt count reaches maxBuildings. (3) Ops: one burn with the burnt set (households as EpochOps.displaced cause fire, placed first at siting; a dossier-backed use relocated first unless a calamity's target; any other use closes cause fire and reopens in this epoch's uses phase with its formerUses bonus); each burnt building decayed at the fire's week with Works CHARRED (§4.11 Works (4)), plot rung-3 eligible, tier (3) rebuilds; a burn burning every building on a timber deck chars the deck to decayed in the same op (V6 §3.19.5 (3)); a masonry deck unharmed. (4) For fire.rebuildYears a rebuild on a burnt plot takes the roof covering fire.rebuildShift steps less flammable where the row admits (our own rule, an extension row, 0 in the parity presets).

Flood (inundate) defaults (a mapped calamity scales depthCm by severity): depthCm 60, collapseDepthCm 80, collapseShare 0.3, timberScourCm 120, spontaneous perYear 0.02 under full on a river or coast town only; flooded land = every ground cell below its nearest water body's flood line (§2.3 flood band) + depthCm; water level = flood line + depthCm; depth at a building = water level − its datum baseCm (§2.2's deriveBase: a deck building's deck surface, V2 §3.16 (5); a terrace building's platform; C6-48; never the raw ground cell); a timber, cob or wattle building at ≥ collapseDepthCm collapses when its draw < collapseShare (→ decay, households displaced, use as fire); a timber deck whose soffit the water passes breaks at collapseShare (V6 §3.19.5 (3)); a timber raised-way support in flooded land with depth at its foot ≥ timberScourCm breaks (V6 §3.19.2 (4)); masonry never breaks this way; underground (ST-45): every gallery or chamber under flooded cells that V04's water rule reaches (ceiling within surfaceClearCm, V4 §4.3) takes the base's flood op (§4.11 DeclineOp) where V4 §2.3 admits (floor below the water table), else reported W_VOID_UNDER_WATER, drawn in the hazards batch cause rule:flood (epoch and hand floods reach the same elements; deep catacombs stay dry); a flood is not a terrain change.

Collapse (topple), event only: params.count (default 1) structures in the given area (x, y, radiusM, default the town) weighted height × (1.5 worn, 2 neglected) × (2 abandoned) on the town-root stream: a building → ruin directly (Works COLLAPSED), households displaced; a wall tower → breach of the stretch around it (up to 20 m each side); a raised-way support → support ruined and both spans beside it ruined (breach) in the same op, their arch vaults collapsing (V6 §3.19.2 (4)); a support whose spans carry a way in use is a candidate only when the break leaves every gate and plot a path (§5.3), filtered before the draw (J-V6.7).

No war: no siege or war operator (item 8: the owner's war example is not written into the design); a dossier calamity of that kind maps to none; it reaches the map only through the fires or collapses the dossier reports, a ConditionOverlay (§4.11 Works (10)), and the population, slices and F5 targets.

Raising the ground (II.7.6's raiseGrade, 'applied by an epoch'; C6-18): after a burn whose burnt set holds a connected region (spread adjacency) of ≥ raise.fireBuildings (60) buildings, or an inundate whose collapsed share exceeds raise.floodShare (0.3) over ≥ raise.minHa (1 ha), raiseGrade fires on that region (the union of struck plots, simplified) when the hazard's next draw on the town-root stream < raise.chance (0.3); operator, buried system and Works are II.7.6's (V04's buried-system builder serves it at an epoch, V04 §3.5); households already in the ledger; buried streets and rooms join the underground (under.access tests them the same epoch); chronicled terrain; dossier-bound only for a mapped calamity.

Terrain and water over epochs (item 25): the base owns kinds, repair and trigger chances (§4.11 Terrain and water change slowly); this section fixes candidates and effects; the terrainWater phase visits candidates in address order, each firing at most once per body per epoch. siltReach: (a) a harbour basin with no live harbour use for silt.idleYears; (b) a reach within silt.downstreamM below a course change or canal off-take since its last silting; (c) an oxbow; the share is the row's; a basin below the harbour draught closes its harbour use (read next epoch). reclaim: a marsh LandUse face or foreshore margin touching a live plot or within 50 m, when S5d's shortfall of the last growth is positive and the face's band is modest or above; region the whole face ≤ reclaim.maxHa else its part within reclaim.bufferM of built land clipped to maxHa from the built side; a shoreline change an enceinte relies on recorded in surfaceChanged and re-evaluated next epoch; under.access tests changed faces the same epoch.

shiftCourse: a reach whose sinuosity between two control knots exceeds river.cutoffSinuosity: the neck = knot pair with the smallest straight distance per metre of course, ≤ 120 m apart; the cut-off re-traces the reach as the chord and the old loop becomes an oxbow (still water body kind oxbow, the abandoned channel, BCR-V6-6, crossings kept, its bridges standing over still water until the lottery's deck candidate clears them once silted to marsh with no occupied deck plot); changed banks enter the scope; an aqueduct's source silted or moved away is read by the raisedWays step the same epoch (runs dry at once, V6 §3.19.2 (2)); avulsion: a reach whose flood cells exceed the row's share re-traces between two knots along the least-cost path through its flood band's lowest ground (deviation ≤ 300 m), the abandoned channel a marsh face; both run as S1's water operator on the changed reach (§7.3 (b)); an oxbow silts to marsh after its oxbow.marshAfterYears (drawn once at formation on stream(EVO_TERRAIN, oxbow)) as a siltReach candidate, shore shrunk by the row's share, below 0.1 ha its water face removed and land typed marsh; digCanal only when a live canal-class use has no canal within its plot's reach: traced on the S3 lattice from the nearest river reach or harbour with existingFabricCost (§4.3), ≤ canal.maxM, no path no canal (reported); the dig is carve (§4.11).

Works (item 67): the works phase (step 18) is the one place the engine creates Works, after every other phase has committed. (1) Which ops start a Works: every building-level physical change of steps 2-15 (build, rebuild, reuse … build, demolish, clear, robStone, a vacate's decay, a strike's decay and ruin, burn (CHARRED in its fire's week), topple's ruin, a repair reoccupy from derelict, every MutationPlan step, rung-2 densify … back_court and thin, rung-3 subdivide or amalgamate (plots in transition, Works (7)), a relet re-cutting a stored plan (convert REFIT)); walls, ways, water and land uses take no Works (J-V6.31), nor raised parts, retaining walls and decks (C6-44; J-V6.90) — drawn at their effective week; buildings on deck plots keep their Works (V2 §3.16).

(2) Start weeks: the first change on a target in an epoch starts at the offset drawn first on the works concern (§6.1), uniform over (prevWeek, week] (Works (10)); a hazard's changes at the hazard's week; a later change on the same target in the same epoch chains, starting the week after the earlier Works reaches FINISHED (or for an instant CHARRED the week after the fire), duration drawn on works, possibly after the epoch's week; a chained Works not started when a later change reaches its target is removed (C6-36): its change stands drawn finished from its own effective week and the later change's Works starts from the stage the prior started Works reached. (3) Across epochs the base's one-target rule holds except a MutationPlan's next step chains after a still-running previous step. (4) Part programmes: a designation whose WorksTable rows name parts starts each part's Works when the previous reaches works.partStartAt (ROOFED), in programme order (Works (3)).

(5) Retirement (BCR-V6-2): the phase retires every Works finished more than works.retainWeeks before the epoch's span start (prevWeek), so the model after an epoch holds every Works that ran during its span (scrub from one model; at 52-week cadence ≈ one more year of finished Works). (6) Restraint and conditions: the share of stock under Works follows the epoch's rate (Works (10)); a ConditionOverlay the port fills scales the share of this epoch's changes started as Works, the rest applied finished. (7) Displaced people: a demolition's or fire's households enter the ledger and are housed by siting in the same epoch (BCR-V6-17); between their old home's EMPTIED (or fire's week) and new home's FINISHED the week-derived occupancy (§10.3) shows them moving, derived never stored.

People over time (§10.3; J-V6.34), derived and costless at an epoch: (1) slots: a household of members n has n slots, slot k's first person ordinal k, birth epoch 0; (2) lifespan: derivePerson gains two appended draws after every existing draw (BCR-V6-10): lifespanYears uniform in its ancestry row's lifespan (default [45, 80]; our own) and entryAge (0 with weight 0.6, else uniform [16, 30]; calibratable); (3) succession: death week = birthWeek + round(52 × lifespanYears) (birthWeek = entry week − 52 × age then); the slot passes to ordinal k + n × j, the successor keyed by that death week as its birth week (bornWeek in place of birth epoch, BCR-V6-10), entering at entryAge — cadence-independent (C6-35); shown dead from the first drawn week at or after its death week; a slot's chain computed on demand by walking successions (O(successions)), never at an epoch; (4) ageing = (week − birthWeek) ÷ 52 at the drawn week; (5) a relocating household keeps its address and people; one that leaves takes them; members change by table-driven re-derivation only; (6) a pinned or edited person is a fixed input, never ended (past lifespan marked 'held past their years', offering to release); the dossier's notables (DR22, staged) never succeeded.

Report and chronicle: each phase returns its EpochReport fragment; close merges them into the EpochReport (joins §5.4's derived report, BCR-V6-14) and writes the chronicle entries, each citing its cause: stage, circuit, gateOpened (counted), wallFate, wallManned, contraction, fire/flood/topple, decline (district households fell ≥ chronicle.declineShare), regrowth (reoccupations ≥ regrowthShare), redevelopment, useOpened/useClosed/useMoved (class significance ≥ significanceMin, else one counted line per district), mutation, terrain (raiseGrade among them), island and underground per participant state change, dossier (with change id, item 75), rename, waterfront, harbourChain, split, merge, ladder, accessOpened (naming its cause), voidSealed, excavated, voidSettled, voidVacated, catacombFounded, catacombStagnant (with block), catacombResumed, catacombsAboveCount, cryptDug, cryptCapped (naming the outranking seat), cryptJoined, raisedWay (founded, finished, repaired, run dry, first held above cap; fallen spans per way), retainingSlump (per district), deck (struck or repaired); ordered by week, kind order, address; text drawn at display from V6 §5.2's templates, never stored.

Frames — the town at any week: locate(w) (J-V6.36): after the last epoch's week the current model; at or before creation the creation prefix's (a rebased document's rebase point); otherwise the model after the first epoch whose week ≥ w (it holds every change and every Works of its span, BCR-V6-2) drawn at w mid-transition; changes without a Works carry an effective week (engine op its epoch's week; dated dossier change its own; hand edit its event's), and the frame applies the before image of every such change of its epoch whose effective week falls after w (C6-16); events between epochs are in the prefix; the frame builder (generation worker) uses the cheapest of a cached HistoryFrame (LRU, device setting), the images path (from the nearest cached frame, keyframe or current model applying HistoryStore images backward/forward, touched chunks' indexes rebuilt, §3.3), or the replay path (from the nearest checkpoint or keyframe folding forward, §7.3 item 2's replay mode, images captured).

Images written at every commit; the verification replay after a load (§12.6) rebuilds them; past the device store setting they spill to the app's disk cache and are fetched on demand; if gone the replay path serves; a keyframe is a copy-on-write chunk table taken every history.checkpointStride-th epoch kept while memory allows (oldest dropped first; output never depends on it); a frame's display is a DisplayDelta from the frame on screen (§8.1). Then and now (3.15.3): diff(w1, w2) lists entities whose lifecycle block has an entry between the two frames' log positions (added, removed, changed with event kinds), derived never stored, removed geometry from the earlier frame; feeds live.history and the clerk.

Timeline bar: spans creation to current week (standalone: the planned trajectory's end as a dashed tail); marks the HistoryIndex epochs, dated events, significant chronicle entries and forks; dragging sets the per-viewer week view key (§2.9); the base's scrub rule (Works (9)) is used only when no epoch event lies in (w, now], otherwise the frame of locate(w) draws — both outside every digest; while the thumb moves the nearest cached frame is shown and the exact frame replaces it when the pointer settles (120 ms, as §12.6's previews).

History across a rebase and an upgrade (C6-15): before a rebase point the document replays from base.state and is not seed-reproducible before base.seq; the timeline greys the range; locate for an earlier week returns the rebased state with 'history before year N was condensed'; forkAt and rerunFrom at an earlier seq bend (J-VI.4; ST-35) to the earliest seq ('history before year N was condensed; the copy starts at year N'); pre-rebase chronicle and EpochReports stay in the saved non-canonical report block (never dropped; BCR-V6-14); why rows survive on lifecycle events; upgrading a history document: replay with a per-epoch diff (HistoryDiff over the two replays' frames with differing chronicle lines) or stay pinned; a document whose epochs carried dossier events stays pinned unless the host asks (HostContext's upgrade request, V08); an upgrade rebuilds reports, store and masks; the strategy read at each epoch's log position.

Determinism stage ids (BCR-V6-8, appended, never renumbered): EVO_PRELUDE, EVO_HAZARD, EVO_FIELD, EVO_USES, EVO_DEPARTURES, EVO_DECLINE, EVO_FORT, EVO_TERRAIN, EVO_LADDER, EVO_MUTATION, EVO_SITING, EVO_GROWTH, EVO_WORKS, EVO_UNDER (the underground adapters' excavation-by-demand draw), EVO_RAISED (raisedWays phase; its gate draws stay the base raised-way stream's keyed by the reason key; SCC-R1C-6); the underground's per-element draws keep V04's keys on the sewer concern (item 109 (j) (3)); participants register their volume's stage (SKY for sky.islands and sky.clearance; S9b for hood.fabric; U-FADE for the four under.* adapters; VS1, VS2, VS8 for village.plan, village.density, village.pins), their draws using that id and table reads recorded under it (V11 §3.1 Readers, T-V11-1 (b); SCC-R2C-11); concerns are the base's: epoch.transform for every engine draw except use.relocate, works, siting and plot.*, siteplan*, S5 concerns, people, naming; no concern added.
