(8) The commit and its reason: committed through the hand operator's event (T4 road with raised for viaduct or elevated road, the aqueduct class for an aqueduct), cause rule:raisedWay, lineage its reason key, the base record's reason set, its arch-vault chambers laid in the commit (C4-110-3) and reconciled by under.extend; the creation event writes detail.why (BCR-V6-20) ≤ 5 rows: reason row (raisedWays.<kind>, family reason, share the strength), condition rows (family condition: drop and metres saved; the rise below the lower anchor with the two endpoints as other; the need ratio with source and terminal as other), gate row (family gate, share p); report raised.founded; chronicle raisedWay.

The rows the pass reads (ST-40; X-V11-11: V06 keeps no copy): V11 §3.24.2's raisedWays table (chance, cap, pMax per rung and kind) and settings (totalCap; viaduct.minDropM, .spanCostFactor, .maxSpanM, .routeClasses; elevated.minRiseM, .maxSpanM, .bandFactor, .landmarkFactor, .landmarkMax, .highGroundM; aqueduct.sourceReachKm, .needRatioMin, .minFallPerKm, .gradient, .capPerSizeMember, .terminal) with its 'chance, stated once'; era and culture factors (V11 §3.19.1, §3.20.3); V11 §3.24.7 (3)-(4) for the dossier's water system and landmarks; V11 §3.18's structures block for disuse and slump cells (SCC-14); the rung gate never a cell; the one row not V11's is raised.stripMarginM (1 m; V1C-68 (2)), the base's row when item 110 lands.

The cap and the count (item 110 (f); C6-40; J-V6.86, J-V6.95): (1) the cap bounds foundations, never survivals: a kind's count = standing generated + suppressed keys + declared; the rung's total = sum; a new way admitted only while its kind's count < its cap and the total < the rung's total cap; decline, prosperity fall, sinking need or a rung fall removes none; above a cap after a rung change reported raised.aboveCap (per kind and total), chronicled once, founding none of that kind until below. (2) Declared ways count (a user's T4 raised way or aqueduct, a skeleton file's): the generator fills only what the author has not built (item 20 (h) analogue of N_c − D_c); never removed by the engine, never making the city 'above cap' in the report; a declared way whose reading gives a suppressed key holds it (counted once); the dossier declares no arches (C6-47).

(3) Standing and released: a generated way counts as standing while repairable (every span standing or ruined, none cleared; every support standing or ruined; the way in use or abandoned; TR-15); once a span is dismantled or a support cleared the way is released: no longer counted or a repair target, its remaining supports and spans ruins the pool clears on salvage demand, its reason key re-opens with the same fixed u — a new way founded by (C) only when its reason is live again, minted with §6.3's collision suffix, its course solver costing the old ruins as ruined footprints (J-V6.95); while a way stands, regrowth-first holds: (B) repairs before (C) admits any new reason. (4) Guards (V12 §3.7.4 owner-rule bars; X19): raised.generatedBelowCity (exactly 0 foundings at TOWN or village-rung epochs, carried ways exempt); raised.reasonMissing (0 generated ways without a reason and its why rows); raised.overCap (0 foundings leaving a kind's count or the total above its cap). (5) Hand-offs: V07's hand-down and hand-up rewrite no event (V7C-43), so a carried way keeps reason, spans and state and suppressions cross in the log; (C) never runs at a village rung and from the first CITY epoch counts declared and carried ways.

Raised ways in disuse, decline, repair (C4-110-2; C5-53; C6-41; J-V6.87, J-V6.94): (1) only generated ways decay by disuse; a declared way is held (item 101 R13), breaking only by a hazard or the landfall, repaired by hand (T4 inspector 'repair'). (2) Lapse and disuse in (A) per standing generated way (address order): lapse condition — viaduct or elevated road: its carried way downgraded (or retired, read as downgraded; TR-03) or neither end's foot junction has an incident part-0 way fronting an occupied plot (a viaduct carrying a primary never lapses by the second test); aqueduct: r < 1; underuseSince (BCR-V6-25) set to the epoch's week by setAttr (author engine) when it first holds, cleared when it ends; disused at once when its carried way was downgraded, else when (week − underuseSince) ÷ 52 reaches streets.abandonAfterYears (viaduct, elevated) or V11 §3.18's aqueduct.disuseAfterYears (SCC-14, SCC-84); a disused way takes neglect (existence abandoned) in this step, chronicled, counted raised.disused; an aqueduct runs dry at once when its source is lost (the spring silted dry or the river moved or silted away from the intake by siltReach or shiftCourse): neglect this step, its terminal's supply off at once (r rises from this epoch), chronicled 'the aqueduct runs dry', counted raised.ranDry.

(3) The strike (pool's raised kind, rate 0.05, BCR-V6-26 persistence row): an abandoned way's candidates weighted w = E(x) · rate · u at the span's midpoint, fabric cap of that district: each standing span whose dwell band has run since the way's neglect (drawn once per span keyed with the neglect's epoch) → breach on its SpanRef, weight × min(1, 0.2 + demand ÷ yield) (deck and arch fall ruined, rubble stays); a ruined span's rubble with salvage demand → dismantle on the span (stone credited, span cleared), weight × min(1, demand ÷ yield), never without demand; a support both of whose spans are ruined or cleared, with salvage demand → dismantle on the support (cleared) — supports outlast spans (a ruined aqueduct stands for centuries as a row of piers); a span or support whose fall would cut a gate's or plot's only path (§5.3) filtered before the draw (J-V6.7); arch-vault chambers collapse with the span in the same batch (breach and dismantle carry V04's collapse, BCR-V6-26).

(4) Hazards: topple takes a support by height and breaks both spans beside it; inundate at a timber support's foot reaching timberScourCm breaks it at collapseShare (masonry never); a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers whatever their state (the island's law; C5-53 (1)), sky.islands records them in scope.raised so this epoch's raisedWays reads an aqueduct's lost supply at once; a hazard breaks a way in use too. (5) Repair, regrowth-first (in (B) before (C)): each standing generated way abandoned or with a ruined span whose reason is live again (aqueduct: source sound and r ≥ needRatioMin; viaduct or elevated: carried way in its class and in use again via upgradeWay or reopenWay and one foot junction fronting an occupied plot) is repaired in address order: repairRaised on each ruined span (its ruined supports with it), then on the way (in use), each on the span district's fabric cap; a refused span waits, the way abandoned until its last span is repaired; a way struck this epoch repaired from the next epoch; a dismantled span or cleared support never rebuilt (released); V04's vaults re-laid by under.extend's reconcile; while a route's viaduct has a ruined span the standing ground course carries its traffic. (6) Chronicle and report: raisedWay lines (founding 'an aqueduct is raised from {cause} to {district}', finish, repair, run-dry, first epoch above a cap, one counted line per way per epoch for fallen spans); the report's raised section.

A removal holds (item 110 (b), (f); C6-38; J-V6.83): the base's collision rule (§6.3) mints fresh over a tombstone and at an epoch the user's delete stands earlier in the log than the generator, so a tombstone alone cannot hold a removal: (1) a delete of a raised way whose lifecycle cause is a generation or epoch rule carries detail.suppress {kind raised, key, reason} (BCR-V6-24), written by the delete operator whatever the source (V9 §4.3's delete, clerk, CLI); (2) every generator reads it: the ledger's suppressed set is the log's live removals; S4, S6, a new stage's S5b and the pass skip a suppressed key and count it filled against its kind's cap and the total (no replacement elsewhere).

(2) The pass reports when the city would have rebuilt it (SR3-10; XV-V9-28; J-V6.120): in (C) a suppressed key is read and gated as any other (its uniform W59's keyed draw, so no other draw moves) and goes no further; each epoch its reading is met and gate passes, one entry {removal (the live delete's seq), week (that removal's week)} in raised.suppressedFired, in removal order; a key a user's re-add serves adds none (its declared way holds it, reading standing); a lifted removal none; TOWN or village-rung epochs none; S4, S6 and S5b skip without an entry; suppressed keys read at every epoch even under V6 §6.1's over-budget fallback; V9 §4.10's epoch row draws one info.raised.suppressed line per entry ({w} the week; Show on the removed way's former outline from the delete event and its tombstone) — V08 §4.6 item 3's line; derived with the report, rebuilt by replay.

(3) What lifts it: only the delete's undo or a forkAt before the removal; what serves it: the user's own re-add serving that reason (a T4 raised way or aqueduct, drawWay {raised: true, class, widthCm, points} or the aqueduct class, the form V9 §4.20.3 (4)'s Build it again emits on the former course) whose reading applied to its ends gives the suppressed key holds the key while it stands, counted once as declared; deleting it leaves the removal in force. (4) Across rungs and hand-offs the removal is kept (in the log). (5) Re-runs: rerunFrom lists the removal among hand edits with re-apply, resolved by the reason key: a way of that key standing in the fork is deleted with its suppression; none standing → reported 'the aqueduct this removal named was never built in this history' with the alternative 'keep the city from building one' (advanced panel's raisedWays rows, item 101 R2), never a silent skip. (6) The dry run: 'The city will not rebuild this aqueduct; undo brings it back.' with fates (arch vaults deleted; for a viaduct the route's standing course carrying its traffic; for an aqueduct the terminal losing supply 'the fountain in {square} runs dry').

(7) The same rule for other re-adding generators: a generated harbour-mouth chain (key enceinte + harbour basin) and quay wall (enceinte + waterfront's water body); a generated retaining wall (its chain's lineage address; the levelling's re-derivation and restoration skip it); a generated deck plot (deck host's id, item 246, and slot ordinal from the host's first end; tier (5) skips that slot; ST-15); each counted held while no re-add serves it, lifted only by the delete's undo or a forkAt before; served by Build it again's (and V10's Put it back, via ClerkMount.rebuildEvents; SR3-08; J-V6.116) forms, keys unchanged: quay wall — drawWall {kind, points, closed} of the removed kind on its former line (served while a declared wall of that kind walls the key's waterfront arc); harbour-mouth chain — placeGate {enceinte, at} at its former place (served while a declared water gate of that enceinte stands across that basin's mouth); retaining wall — drawWall {kind retaining, points, closed, highSide} on its former chain (served while a declared retaining wall's chain lies on the removed chain's line first to last vertex); deck plot — drawFootprint {polygon, cls?} on the deck whose plot S11 fits at slot k (served while that declared plot stands at (host, k)); a served key never generated again while its re-add stands, counted once as declared, never in suppressedHeld; deleting the re-add leaves the removal in force; a tombstone keyed by the line alone would not hold (§6.3 re-mints); islands and sky accesses keep V05's record form under the same lift rule (f item 260).

Retaining walls over epochs (item 110 (a); C6-42; J-V6.88): (1) generated RetainingWalls made or re-derived only by an op that levels (a new stage's S10-S11 on new faces; a rung-3 re-cut or a rebuild/reuse … build running S11 on its plot — a footprint-keeping rebuild does not re-level; raiseGrade, under which each wall inside the raised region is tombstoned in the raiseGrade batch (cause convert:raiseGrade; ST-34) and V04's buried-system builder reads it as a step in the buried floor, storey chambers on its high side at its high-side datum (V4 §3.5.5), and new ones derived on the new grade); a suppressed wall never made or re-derived (retaining.suppressedHeld); no epoch re-derives a standing wall whose plots it did not re-level (T-V6-3); levelled plots and blocks with walls enter EpochScope.levelled; report retaining.created, .rederived, .buried. (2) No plot operation deletes one (amalgamate only across wall-free boundaries else plotToGarden; plotToGarden keeps the wall; rung-3 re-cut and absorbWall's S10 re-cut keep it as a fixed line).

(3) Slump as their own candidate (pool's retaining kind, rate 0.05, BCR-V6-26): a generated wall cut into stretches of retaining.stretchM from its first vertex; a standing stretch is a candidate when every plot on its high side within retaining.holdM has been empty, garden, orchard or field for retaining.neglectAfterYears (V11 §3.18's cells; SCC-14, SCC-84), read from the plots' lifecycle blocks, the span keyed with the epoch the last emptied; a strike breaches the stretch to decayed (no edge removed, no terrain change; C5-53 (2)); dismantle takes a decayed stretch's stone only on salvage demand (→ ruined, bank remains); a drawn wall held; chronicled retainingSlump per district; report retaining.slumped. (4) Crossings keep their steps: downgradeWay keeps a crossing's stair or ramp (an interval attribute; V1C-66), upgradeWay restores the class with the same crossing. (5) Plans and the sewer: in an epoch that levels an unstored plan beside levelled faces goes stale and a stored one is re-cut inside the epoch event (BCR-V3-28; T-V3-30; V3C-71 (4); TU-06 (c)); under.extend takes U-NET's invert drops at wall crossings of ways in scope.levelled (C4-110-7).

(6) Restoration (ST-10; J-V6.101): a decayed stretch of a generated wall re-derived intact by a repairRetaining in the restoring op's batch, by (a) any epoch op re-levelling a plot on its high side within retaining.holdM (a tier (3) rebuild or reuse … build running S11, a rebuild on a house platform (V07 §3.12), a rung-3 re-cut) — cause rule:regrowth, fabric cap of the stretch's district; (b) the landfall clearance (cause rule:landfall); a ruined stretch not restored (stone gone): the re-levelling lays a new stretch on its line (successor lineage, §6.3), the ruined one tombstoned in the same batch; a drawn wall restored only by hand (T3 inspector repair), a ruined drawn stretch bending to a new drawn stretch (J-VI.4); a suppressed wall never restored; counted retaining.restored.

Decks over epochs (item 110 (d); C6-43; J-V6.89): (1) offering: an epoch builds a deck only through a new stage's S5c bridge at an unused crossing site (§4.11) or a new stage's S7 harbour furniture, and restores one only by repairRaised's deck form; deck faces (mole, pier, quay platform, bridge deck) offered at regrowth tier (5), cut by S10's deck rule under V11 §3.24.4's deck table as V2 §3.16 reads it (ST-51); tier (4) and the use phase admit only deckOk uses (effective crypt first; SCC-31); a suppressed deck slot skipped (decks.suppressedHeld); counted decks.offered. (2) The budget binds every epoch op on a deck plot (no densify, no rung-2 back_court; relet within capacity; MutationPlan steps and rebuilds through S11's capped mutator, V2 §3.16 (3); rung 3's subdivide and amalgamate inside the deck's width).

(3) Striking a deck (pool's deck kind, rate 0.08, BCR-V6-26): a deck is item 246's Plot.deck.host (Bridge for a bridge deck; pier or quay way for mole, pier, quay platform); its condition is the host's lifecycle existence (breach → decayed, ruin → ruined, repairRaised → former existence from the striking op's undo record); Bridge.state untouched (ST-56); a bridge or pier deck is a candidate when its way no longer crosses live water (an oxbow silted to marsh) or its way has been downgraded, and no deck plot on it is occupied; a strike ruins it (ST-38), its way cut there only where §5.3 allows (else no candidate); hazards: a flood whose water level passes a timber deck's soffit breaks it (ruined) at collapseShare; a burn burning every building on a timber deck chars it to decayed (impassable until repaired); masonry neither; a hazard break §5.3 would refuse leaves the deck decayed and standing, reported; a struck deck ruins what stands on it by least disruption in the same batch (buildings ruin, dossier-backed uses relocated first, households displaced cause flood, fire or clearance, deck plots tombstoned with the deck); counted decks.struck, chronicled deck ('the houses on {subject} are swept away'). (4) Rebuilding regrowth-first: in (B) a ruined or decayed deck whose way is still in use and crosses live water is repaired (repairRaised, fabric cap) from the epoch after the one that struck it; faces offered again by (1); buildings on them new lineages (V2 §3.16 (7)); counted decks.repaired.

A dossier-bound document (items 20, 20 (h); C6-47; J-V6.92): raised ways are map-derived (the dossier lists institutions, not arches); runs (A)-(C) as standalone with two limits: the aqueduct's terminal is the water-system record's bound conduit_house when present, else a fountain Pin — never an institution the dossier does not list; a removed generated way is suppressed like any other; the water-system record acts at CITY and METROPOLIS only by V11 §3.24.7 (3) (need counts as met, never a chance factor, SS-13; each SIZE member raising the aqueduct cap and the total by capPerSizeMember; its conduit_house the terminal); never forces arches where no source is in reach (pMax holds; a miss reported aqueduct_no_source); landmarks, era and culture rows are factors; the clearing never touches a dossier-listed building.

Advancing time: T1 intend gains a time card (BCR-V6-11): 'Advance … years', a shape chip (grow, reach, decline, hold, follow the timeline, mapped by V6 §2.3), optional span, cadence, threat and era behind 'more', a hazards chip (none, minor, full; absent on a dossier-bound document), 'start small' at creation; the clerk's tool API gains advance (§11.2); the CLI 'plat advance <doc> --years N --to P / --rate r [--cadence w] [--hazards m]'.

A lone neighbourhood document (V01 J-V1.36; ST-41; J-V6.102): on a hood document (one district's close-up opened alone, no S4-S5 growth route) the time card and 'start small' are absent; the clerk's and CLI's advance bend to none with 'a neighbourhood alone has no history yet — open it in its town to advance time' (item 101 R2); a skeleton file's history block bent likewise; forkAt, the timeline bar over existing events and the history panel still work; 'the gate lifts when volume 6 builds hood epochs (§13's fix list)'.

What advance appends: one group (§7.4) of epoch events, one per cadence step, each folded before the next, each carrying EpochInputs.advance (BCR-V6-9), the trajectory on the first; run as a cancellable background job in the generation worker with a progress bar; Stop ends the job after the running epoch and folded epochs stand as a shorter group; dossier-bound refused (J-V6.2). Preview (item 101 R3, R14): before commit the card and clerk run the whole request on a scratch fork in the background (lower priority than the picture) showing the end state against the present (then-and-now) with a count badge (households and buildings gained or lost, the walled share, raised ways built by kind), the history panel listing raisedWay lines; the clerk offers three variations (logistic, linear, front-loaded), the card one; accept appends the chosen one's epochs; above advance.maxEpochs the card bends the cadence; on a dossier-bound document the card is replaced by 'Make a what-if copy and advance it'.

Undo of an advance (§7.4): the group is one undo step while its last epoch is the latest live event: the undo restores the checkpoint taken before the group's first epoch and truncates the group in an unshared document (needing neither a hundred undo records nor §7.4's 64-event / 20 MB window); per-epoch undo records kept for the group's latest epoch only; after commit the epochs' checkpoints are dropped except every history.checkpointStride-th (the history store's keyframes); an epoch carrying a dossier event is never an undo target (§7.4), so a dossier-bound history is undone only by the host.

Hand forms of the engine's changes (item 101 tools): ring fate and week (T3 inspector chip; setAttr on Enceinte.pathway source edit); ring road now, absorbed wall now, shorter ring (T3 inspector 'make a road', 'build over it', draw a shorter ring; convert wallToWay / absorbWall / contractWall); repair a breach, back in use (T3 grip 'repair', inspector 'back in use'; convert repairWall with or without stretch; dismantled stretch bends to drawWall 'its stone is gone; a new stretch is built here'); let a lane go / bring it back (T4 class chip; convert downgradeWay / upgradeWay; setAttr of class clears formerClass); a fire, flood, collapse (the history panel's hazard tray: spark, flood depth, tap a tower; dry run ghost with three variations keyed by the event's seq and reroll, committed as burn or the resolved decay, flood, ruin, breach ops; one undo step with re-homing and relocations); a field fallow or taken back (T2 land-use chip; convert retypeLand); a use opened, closed, moved (T6 place; convert openUse / closeUse / relocateUse, with mutate … spread 'epochs' from 'over years'); a mutation's pace (T9 inspector: each step's year, 'do it now', 'cancel the plan'; setAttr on MutationPlan.steps[i].dueWeek, mutate with the step, delete of the plan); a failing shop given time (use inspector 'clear its trouble'; setAttr Use.strain absent); the engine's rates (advanced panel evolution rows and params; editTable, adjust; from the next epoch, never re-running history J-V6.28); a future on the timeline ('+ at this year'; §7.7 timeline edits); a scheduled change (startWorks); hold against history (T10 lock / pin).

Hand forms (cont.): quay wall or open waterfront, harbour-mouth chain (T3 inspector 'wall the quays' / 'open front' / 'chain the mouth'; drawWall with sea gates / neglect; the chain as S7 furniture; a declared waterfront held, item 101 R13); shop split or merged (T6 'split into works and shop' / 'merge onto one plot'; openUse with branchOf / closeUse of the shop, cause edit, and the merge-back declaration item 104 (a) (1)); a supply link pinned, moved, cut (V09's link view; map-side link declaration, never written to the dossier); a record's member re-bound or held (T6 inspector 'belongs to Blacksmiths (3-10)', 'keep this one'; assign / pin); an access into a sealed cave or excavation (V04's placeAccess, drawTunnel system dug; addUndergroundAccess closure, §7.3 item 9); a crypt drawn, extended, declared (V03 interior tools 'crypt here', V02 basement ring; V03 setAttr(basement) on basement/crypt/ring, V02 mutate; an author-set ring never trimmed); a catacomb gallery drawn or deleted (V04's drawTunnel/drawChamber system catacomb, delete; a deleted gallery lowers the ratchet's floor); raise the ground ('raise the ground here'; convert raiseGrade, II.7.6); seal or reopen a passage, cleared back building a garden (T5 plot inspector; convert sealPassage / openPassage, reuse as garden).

Hand forms (item 110): add a raised way (T4 road with raised, or the aqueduct class; the base's hand operator's event, cause edit, declared; held; counts toward its cap; a re-add serving a suppressed reason holds that key); remove a generated raised way, harbour-mouth chain, quay wall, retaining wall or deck plot (V9 §4.3's delete, clerk, CLI; delete carrying detail.suppress; dry run 'The city will not rebuild this aqueduct; undo brings it back' / 'The town will not rebuild this terrace wall' / 'No house will be built on this spot of the bridge', with vault, route and terminal fates; undo lifts); build a removed thing again (V9 §4.20.3 (4)'s Build it again where Undo this is refused as dependent; V10's Put it back via ClerkMount.rebuildEvents; the declared re-add filled from the removed thing's last record: drawWay raised or aqueduct class, drawWall, placeGate, drawWall retaining, drawFootprint on the deck; serves the key while it stands, deleting it leaves the removal); repair a raised way or deck (T4 inspector 'repair', 'rebuild the deck'; convert repairRaised; dismantled span or cleared support bends to a new raised part 'rebuilt as a new span'); repair a retaining wall (T3 inspector on a decayed stretch; convert repairRetaining; ruined stretch bends to a new drawn stretch); a retaining wall (T3 retaining, T2 terrace stroke's edge; drawn walls held, never slump); a building on a deck face (T6 place on a deck plot; build / openUse through S11's deck rule; a use deckOk refuses bends to the nearest admitted class — an always-crypt use to land by V09's T6 landward bend; item 101 R2); 'no raised ways in this town' (advanced panel raisedWays chance rows; editTable; from the next epoch, standing ways kept; dry run 'the ways already built stay; remove them one by one if you want them gone').

Edit kinds of every new entity kind (§2.8 registry, BCR-V6-7): MutationPlan (setAttr of a step's dueWeek, delete); Enceinte.pathway (setAttr) and underuseSince (engine-only, derived-by-epoch, cleared by any hand change to the ring's trace); Way.formerClass (engine-only; cleared by setAttr of class); Use.strain (setAttr); BuildingShadeMask (engine-only, derived-by-epoch: a user changes shade by changing casters or the prosperity brush, item 102 (f)); LifecycleEvent.detail.why (engine-only; a hand move writes its own event with no rows, answered 'moved by hand in year N'); Household.transit (engine-only, epoch-local); detail.suppress (written by the delete operator; never edited; the delete's undo lifts it); a raised way's underuseSince (engine-only); span/support state (engine ops and hand repairRaised); retaining stretch state (engine ops and hand repairRetaining); deck condition (engine ops and repairRaised's deck form); the crypt rank's caps, effective week, catacomb primary, excavation reading and RaisedWayLedger are derived with no edit kind.

Locality, locks, order: an epoch's scope is its touched set (§7.3's oracle holds: everything outside its touched set and faces byte-identical; T-V6-3); protection first (locked, pinned, declared entities, assigned ones outside the use rules and a dossier-backed use's building before relocation filtered before any draw or cap; J-V6.7), so holding a thing never shifts which other things the history picks; a removed generated raised way, harbour-mouth chain, quay wall, retaining wall or deck plot held by its suppression (a tombstone alone could not; §6.3); edits between epochs are ordinary events at the head (an edit on an entity with a running Works follows §4.11 Works (1)-(2)); undo across epochs: a standalone epoch undoable while latest, otherwise through §7.4's independence check which an epoch usually fails — the conflict offers 're-run from before it'.

forkAt(seq) (§11.2; BCR-V6-11): a new document with the same recipe and the log prefix through seq, a fresh document id and a forkedFrom {docId, seq, modelDigest} header outside every digest; a fork of a dossier-bound document is detached (keeps its history, no host bridge, no later dossier event; a what-if; the dossier stays the original's sole truth, items 20, 22); a what-if is a fork (fork before the epoch, lock in the copy, advance the copy; rerunFrom with no change reproduces the original, T-V6-22; SR5-09).

rerunFrom(seq): forkAt(seq), then every later epoch or dossier event (EditBase.dossier set, its dossierChange kept) re-appended in log order (epochs from stored EpochInputs, standalone dossier events as they were) and recomputed on the fork's state (a later epoch never names an institution only a dropped dossier event had added, item 20); every other later event (hand edits, locks, table edits, adjusts) listed with 're-apply' re-appending it at the fork's head through the ordinary fold, addresses by §6.3's carry-over matching, an unresolved address returning F-EDIT with closest alternatives (item 101 R2), never silent; a suppressing removal re-applies by its reason key; a detached dossier fork (J-V6.37) re-runs with dossier events as recorded; before a rebase point forkAt and rerunFrom bend to the earliest seq ('history before year N was condensed; the copy starts at year N'); the history panel offers both on any chronicle entry or mark; the clerk offers a copy on 'what if…' and a re-run when asked (V10 prompt rule 17; SR5-03).

terminology.where: V06 passim (889 'V6 §n' self-pointers; 103 single-digit pointers to other volumes: V2 14, V4 38, V5 26, V9 25; 28 'V1-x' labels; bare '§3.x' for own sections in §2.2's table (header 'V6 section') and in the ledgers and notes)
terminology.claim: V06 names itself 'V6 §n' (the base and V05's base requests write 'V06 §n'), points to other volumes with single-digit prefixes ('V4 §3.10', 'V5 §3.16', 'V9 §4.20.3', 'V2 §3.16') beside the 'V0n §n' form it also uses, and cites its own sections bare in §2.2's table, where bare '§3.6', '§3.7.1', '§3.12' are also base section numbers (the kernel's §3.6, §3.7 …) — one concept, several pointer forms, and bare pointers that resolve to a different base section.
terminology.hint: Normalise to the set's one pointer form ('V06 §n' for this volume, 'V0n §n' for others, bare § only for the base) and prefix §2.2's table references.
